[tool.poetry]
name = "dotmac-learning"
version = "0.1.0a1"
description = "Reusable tenant learning results, progress, completion and certificates"
authors = ["DotMac"]
readme = "README.md"
packages = [
    { include = "dotmac_learning", from = "src" },
    { include = "dotmac_learning_bank_rules", from = "src" },
]
include = [
    { path = "src/dotmac_learning_bank_rules/py.typed", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] },
    { path = "src/dotmac_learning/py.typed", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] },
    { path = "src/dotmac_learning/migrations/**/*", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] },
]

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
# Published tenant-audit prerequisite; hosted floor qualification is required.
dotmac-kernel = ">=0.1.0a106"
sqlalchemy = "^2.0"
pydantic = "^2.9"
alembic = ">=1.13"

[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"

[tool.poetry]
name = "dotmac-fulfillment"
version = "0.1.0a2"
description = "DotMac tenant-scoped fulfillment saga, participant attempt, outcome, compensation, and convergence ownership"
authors = ["DotMac"]
readme = "README.md"
packages = [{ include = "dotmac_fulfillment", from = "src" }]
include = [
    { path = "src/dotmac_fulfillment/py.typed", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] },
    { path = "src/dotmac_fulfillment/migrations/**/*", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] },
]

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
# a86 minted the `mod_fulfillment` lineage, but this package also consumes the
# typed provisioning participant, scoped request, asynchronous outcome envelope
# and participant-decided compensation contract, which land in a89. Take the
# HIGHEST consumed capability, then the first PUBLISHED release carrying it:
# a106 additionally supplies the tenant-audit prerequisite consumed by this release.
# It is published, independently registry-verified and tagged.
dotmac-kernel = ">=0.1.0a106"
sqlalchemy = "^2.0"

[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"

[tool.poetry]
name = "dotmac-template-studio"
version = "0.2.0a6"
description = "DotMac Template Studio — tenant-authored notification and document templates (ADR-0006 M1, the first stateful module)"
authors = ["DotMac"]
readme = "README.md"
packages = [{ include = "dotmac_template_studio", from = "src" }]
include = [
    # PEP 561 marker — the module's contracts are annotated, and a consuming
    # assembly's type-checker cannot see them without this.
    { path = "src/dotmac_template_studio/py.typed", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] },
    # The admin screens. Package data, NOT assembly files: a module is
    # pip-installed, so its Jinja lives outside any assembly's template root and
    # is composed through the manifest's namespaced `TemplatePackage`.
    { path = "src/dotmac_template_studio/templates/**/*", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] },
    # The module's OWN Alembic lineage (prefix `ts`, branch label
    # `template_studio`), composed by a consuming assembly through
    # `version_locations`. No `__init__` in versions/ (Alembic convention), so
    # it is declared explicitly as package data.
    { path = "src/dotmac_template_studio/migrations/**/*", format = ["sdist", "wheel"] },
]

[tool.poetry.dependencies]
# Floor 3.11 to match the kernel and the products that consume it.
python = ">=3.11,<3.14"
# The primary runtime dependency, and the direction ADR-0006 § 2 fixes: this
# module may depend on the kernel; it never depends on an assembly, another
# module, or `dotmac-ui`. The assembly composes the UI package independently.
#
# Floors, not preferences — matched to the kernel's own declared floors so
# installing this module cannot force a consumer's FastAPI/SQLAlchemy upgrade.
# Contract-v2 surfaces and namespaced templates first required a97.
# a106 additionally supplies the tenant-audit prerequisite consumed by this release;
# it is published, independently registry-verified and tagged.
dotmac-kernel = ">=0.1.0a106"
fastapi = ">=0.111,<0.116"
sqlalchemy = "^2.0"
pydantic = ">=2.7.4,<3.0"

# Note the absence of `dotmac-ui`. The admin screens author against
# `var(--dmui-*)` tokens, but they consume them as CSS custom properties the
# ASSEMBLY has already loaded (ADR-0006 D3's compiled-asset boundary) — a
# stylesheet link, not a Python import. Declaring the dependency would buy
# nothing and would couple a data-plane module to a presentation release.

[build-system]
requires = ["poetry-core"]
build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api"

"""Typed learning commands and facts in the caller's transaction.

Learning owns results, progress, certificates, curriculum, reading, events,
enrolment, audience classification, tracks, course access, delivery scheduling,
announcements, pacing, gradebook, reports and learner agenda/todo projections.
Products retain authorization, file and presentation adapters, lab execution
and admissions integration. Pure selection, option ordering, validity and grading
reuse the existing engine. Attempt policy, persisted sittings, grants and feedback
reuse the existing source owner; the default result wrapper binds the caller
Session. Importing this surface creates no engine.
"""

"""Learner calendar / agenda service."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from . import scheduling
from .agenda_contracts import AgendaItem, AgendaTarget
from .delivery_models import ClassSession, OfferingActivity
from .entitlements import accessible_course_ids
from .models import Activity, Course
from .participation_models import CourseOffering, Enrollment


def upcoming_for_person(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    limit: int = 50,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> tuple[AgendaItem, ...]:
    """Merged, chronologically-sorted future agenda items for a person.

    Returns offering window open/close events and activity due_at deadlines
    across the person's accessible courses. Past items are excluded.
    Products render kind labels and navigation from detached semantic targets.
    """
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    items: list[AgendaItem] = []
    course_ids = accessible_course_ids(db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id)

    courses_by_id: dict[UUID, Course] = (
        {
            c.id: c
            for c in db.scalars(
                select(Course)
                .where(Course.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                .where(Course.id.in_(course_ids))
            ).all()
        }
        if course_ids
        else {}
    )

    for off in (
        []
        if not course_ids
        else db.scalars(
            select(CourseOffering)
            .where(CourseOffering.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(CourseOffering.status == "active")
            .where(CourseOffering.course_id.in_(course_ids))
        ).all()
    ):
        course = courses_by_id.get(off.course_id)
        if course is None:
            continue
        if off.starts_at is not None and off.starts_at > now:
            items.append(
                AgendaItem(
                    off.starts_at,
                    "opens",
                    course.title,
                    course.title,
                    AgendaTarget("course", course.id, course.slug),
                )
            )
        if off.ends_at is not None and off.ends_at > now:
            items.append(
                AgendaItem(
                    off.ends_at,
                    "closes",
                    course.title,
                    course.title,
                    AgendaTarget("course", course.id, course.slug),
                )
            )

    rows = (
        []
        if not course_ids
        else db.execute(
            select(OfferingActivity, Activity, Course)
            .join(
                Activity,
                (Activity.id == OfferingActivity.activity_id)
                & (Activity.tenant_id == OfferingActivity.tenant_id),
            )
            .join(
                CourseOffering,
                (CourseOffering.id == OfferingActivity.offering_id)
                & (CourseOffering.tenant_id == OfferingActivity.tenant_id),
            )
            .join(
                Course,
                (Course.id == CourseOffering.course_id)
                & (Course.tenant_id == CourseOffering.tenant_id),
            )
            .where(OfferingActivity.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(CourseOffering.status == "active")
            .where(CourseOffering.course_id.in_(course_ids))
            .where(OfferingActivity.due_at.isnot(None))
            .where(OfferingActivity.due_at > now)
        ).all()
    )

    for pa, act, course in rows:
        if pa.due_at is None:
            raise AssertionError
        items.append(
            AgendaItem(
                pa.due_at,
                "due",
                act.title,
                course.title,
                AgendaTarget("activity", act.id),
            )
        )

    # Class sessions on the person's cohort timetable (student or instructor).
    cohort_ids = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(Enrollment.cohort_id)
            .where(Enrollment.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(Enrollment.person_id == person_id)
        ).all()
    )
    if cohort_ids:
        for s in db.scalars(
            select(ClassSession)
            .where(ClassSession.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(ClassSession.cohort_id.in_(cohort_ids))
            .where(ClassSession.status == "scheduled")
            # Keep a session visible until it ends, not until it starts —
            # otherwise a live class vanishes from the calendar at the exact
            # moment the learner needs the Join affordance (join_is_open and
            # scheduling.list_for_person both treat in-progress as current).
            .where(func.coalesce(ClassSession.ends_at, ClassSession.starts_at) >= now)
        ).all():
            session = scheduling._fact(s)
            items.append(
                AgendaItem(
                    s.starts_at,
                    "session",
                    s.title,
                    "",
                    AgendaTarget("session", s.id),
                    session,
                    scheduling.join_is_open(session, now=now),
                )
            )

    items.sort(key=lambda x: x.when)
    return tuple(items[:limit])

"""Caller-transaction announcements with optional product notification fanout."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from uuid import UUID

from dotmac_kernel.audit import write_audit_event
from sqlalchemy import or_, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .announcement_contracts import (
    AnnouncementFact,
    AnnouncementFanout,
    CreateAnnouncementCommand,
    DeleteAnnouncementCommand,
)
from .attempt_contracts import AttemptAuditContext
from .delivery_models import Announcement
from .participation_models import Enrollment
from .results import _transaction, _unchanged

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def _fact(announcement: Announcement) -> AnnouncementFact:
    return AnnouncementFact(
        id=announcement.id,
        tenant_id=announcement.tenant_id,
        cohort_id=announcement.cohort_id,
        author_person_id=announcement.author_person_id,
        title=announcement.title,
        body_md=announcement.body_md,
        body_html=announcement.body_html,
        created_at=announcement.created_at,
        updated_at=announcement.updated_at,
    )


def create(
    db: Session,
    command: CreateAnnouncementCommand,
    *,
    audit_context: AttemptAuditContext,
    fanout: AnnouncementFanout,
) -> AnnouncementFact:
    """Flush the announcement, isolate fanout failure, then require Kernel audit.

    The product supplies rendered HTML and trusted audit attribution. Required
    failures propagate; the caller owns the transaction and any rollback.
    """
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    if audit_context.tenant_id != command.tenant_id:
        raise ValueError("Audit context tenant scope does not match the command.")
    ann = Announcement(
        tenant_id=command.tenant_id,
        cohort_id=command.cohort_id,
        author_person_id=command.author_person_id,
        title=command.title,
        body_md=command.body_md,
        body_html=command.body_html,
    )
    db.add(ann)
    db.flush()

    if command.cohort_id is not None:
        audience_ids = tuple(
            db.scalars(
                select(Enrollment.person_id)
                .where(Enrollment.tenant_id == command.tenant_id)
                .where(Enrollment.cohort_id == command.cohort_id)
                .where(Enrollment.status == "active")
                .where(Enrollment.role_in_cohort == "student")
            ).all()
        )
    else:
        audience_ids = tuple(
            db.scalars(
                select(Enrollment.person_id)
                .where(Enrollment.tenant_id == command.tenant_id)
                .where(Enrollment.status == "active")
                .distinct()
            ).all()
        )
    fact = _fact(ann)
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    if audience_ids:
        try:
            with db.begin_nested():
                fanout(db, fact, audience_ids)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.warning("announcement notify fan-out failed: %s", exc)
    _unchanged(db, boundary)

    write_audit_event(
        db,
        tenant_id=command.tenant_id,
        actor_type=audit_context.actor_type,
        actor_id=audit_context.actor_id,
        actor_label=audit_context.actor_label,
        actor_party_id=command.author_person_id,
        source_application=audit_context.source_application,
        action="announcement.created",
        entity_type="announcement",
        entity_id=str(ann.id),
    )
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return fact


def for_person(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    limit: int = 20,
) -> tuple[AnnouncementFact, ...]:
    """Return tenant-wide announcements and those for any active enrollment."""
    enrolled_cohort_ids = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(Enrollment.cohort_id)
            .where(Enrollment.tenant_id == tenant_id)

def reveal_feedback(
    activity: FeedbackTerms,
    *,
    passed: bool,
    attempts_used: int,
    attempts_granted: int = 0,
) -> bool:

    if mode == "practice":

    ).exhausted

class LearningSnapshotV4:

    version: Literal[4]

    activity_attempts: tuple[ActivityAttemptRowV4, ...]
    attempt_grants: tuple[AttemptGrantRowV4, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if type(self.version) is not int or self.version != 4:
            raise SnapshotValidationError(
                "unsupported twenty-three-table snapshot version"
            )
        _participation_slice(self)
        extent = set(self.tenant_ids)
        for table, row_type in _ASSESSMENT_ROW_TYPES:
            rows = getattr(self, table)
            if type(rows) is not tuple:
                raise SnapshotValidationError(f"storage rows must be a tuple: {table}")
            keys: set[UUID] = set()
            for row in rows:
                if type(row) is not row_type:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"wrong storage row contract: {table}"
                    )
                row.__post_init__()
                if row.tenant_id not in extent:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"storage row outside declared extent: {table}/{row.id}"
                    )
                if row.id in keys:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"duplicate storage key: {table}/{row.id}"
                    )
                keys.add(row.id)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return "LearningSnapshotV4(<twenty-three-table storage rows>)"

"""One owner for how many attempts a learner has, and whether they are spent.

Before this module the question "may this learner sit again?" was answered in
five places, each spelling the same expression by hand::

    activity.max_attempts is not None and used >= activity.max_attempts

``assessment.submit_activity`` used it to refuse a submission,
``assessment.reveal_feedback`` to decide whether the answer key may be shown,
``learner_dashboard`` to render "1 of 3 attempts left", ``success_queue`` to
flag a stuck learner, and ``insights`` to report ``attempts_exhausted``. All
five agreed only because none of them had changed yet.

Granting an extra attempt is what breaks that. An entitlement that lives on
``Activity.max_attempts`` alone cannot express "this learner, this activity,
one more go" — so the moment grants exist, every one of those five expressions
is wrong in a different way. The dashboard would promise a retake the submit
path refuses, or the submit path would allow one the answer key had already
been revealed for, which hands back a graded attempt the learner has the
answers to.

So the entitlement is computed here, once, and the five callers ask.

See ``docs/adr/0005-assessment-engine-owns-exam-logic.md`` — this is the same
correction one layer down from selection and validity: a decision with several
implementations drifts as soon as any of them moves.
"""

from uuid import UUID

class ActivityTerms(Protocol):

class BoundGrantReader(Protocol):
    """Read the grant total for an already-bound learner and activity."""

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Entitlement:
    """What a learner may still do on one activity.

    ``limit`` is None for an uncapped activity, in which case nothing is ever
    exhausted and ``remaining`` is None rather than a large number — callers
    render "unlimited", and a number would invite them to count down from it.
    """

    used: int
    granted: int
    limit: int | None

    @property
    def remaining(self) -> int | None:
        if self.limit is None:
            return None
        return max(self.limit - self.used, 0)

    @property
    def exhausted(self) -> bool:
        return self.limit is not None and self.used >= self.limit


def granted_for(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, activity_id: UUID
) -> int:
    """Extra attempts this learner has been granted on this activity."""
    return int(
        db.scalar(
            select(func.coalesce(func.sum(AttemptGrant.extra_attempts), 0))
            .where(AttemptGrant.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(AttemptGrant.activity_id == activity_id)
            .where(AttemptGrant.person_id == person_id)
        )
        or 0
    )


def granted_by_activity(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID
) -> dict[UUID, int]:
    """Grants per activity for one learner, in ONE grouped query.

    The dashboard and the success queue both render every activity on a course
    at once; asking per activity would turn one page into N queries.
    """
    rows = db.execute(
        select(AttemptGrant.activity_id, func.sum(AttemptGrant.extra_attempts))
        .where(AttemptGrant.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(AttemptGrant.person_id == person_id)
        .group_by(AttemptGrant.activity_id)
    ).all()
    return {activity_id: int(n or 0) for activity_id, n in rows}


def entitlement(activity: ActivityTerms, *, used: int, granted: int = 0) -> Entitlement:
    """The pure part: what the limit is, given the counts.

    Separate from the queries so callers that have already batched their counts
    — the dashboard, the success queue — reuse the same arithmetic without
    going back to the database per activity.
    """
    limit = None if activity.max_attempts is None else activity.max_attempts + granted
    return Entitlement(used=used, granted=granted, limit=limit)


def entitlement_with_grants(
    activity: ActivityTerms, *, used: int, reader: BoundGrantReader
) -> Entitlement:
    """Apply the shared arithmetic to terms and one bound grant read."""
    return entitlement(activity, used=used, granted=reader.total())


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _LearnerGrantReader:
    db: Session
    tenant_id: UUID
    person_id: UUID
    activity_id: UUID

    def total(self) -> int:
        return granted_for(
            self.db,
            tenant_id=self.tenant_id,
            person_id=self.person_id,
            activity_id=self.activity_id,
        )


def for_learner(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, activity: ActivityFact, used: int
) -> Entitlement:
    """The entitlement, fetching this learner's grants."""
    reader = _LearnerGrantReader(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, activity_id=activity.id
    )
    return entitlement_with_grants(activity, used=used, reader=reader)


def grant_extra_attempt(
    db: Session,
    payload: GrantExtraAttemptCommand,
    *,
    audit_context: AttemptAuditContext,
) -> AttemptGrantFact:
    """Append a grant and its required canonical Kernel audit in caller scope."""
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    if audit_context.tenant_id != payload.tenant_id:
        raise ValueError("attempt audit context scope does not match command")
    if payload.extra_attempts < 1:
        raise ValueError("a grant must add at least one attempt")
    if not (payload.reason or "").strip():
        raise ValueError("a grant must record why it was given")
    row = AttemptGrant(
        tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
        person_id=payload.person_id,
        activity_id=payload.activity_id,
        reason=payload.reason.strip(),
        granted_by=payload.granted_by,
        extra_attempts=payload.extra_attempts,
    )
    db.add(row)
    db.flush()
    write_audit_event(
        db,
        tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
        actor_type=audit_context.actor_type,
        actor_id=audit_context.actor_id,
        actor_label=audit_context.actor_label,
        source_application=audit_context.source_application,
        actor_party_id=payload.granted_by,
        action="attempt_granted",
        entity_type="activity",
        entity_id=str(payload.activity_id),
        details={
            "person_id": str(payload.person_id),
            "extra_attempts": payload.extra_attempts,
            "reason": row.reason,
        },
    )
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return AttemptGrantFact(
        **{name: getattr(row, name) for name in AttemptGrantFact.__dataclass_fields__}
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BoundAttemptPolicy:
    """The source grant reader bound to this exact caller Session and scope."""

    db: Session
    tenant_id: UUID
    person_id: UUID
    activity_id: UUID

    def evaluate(self, observation: AdmissionObservation) -> AdmissionDecision:
        boundary = _transaction(self.db)
        if (observation.tenant_id, observation.person_id, observation.activity_id) != (
            self.tenant_id,
            self.person_id,
            self.activity_id,
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "attempt admission observation scope does not match policy"
            )
        reader = _LearnerGrantReader(
            self.db, self.tenant_id, self.person_id, self.activity_id
        )
        allowed = not entitlement_with_grants(
            observation, used=observation.used, reader=reader
        ).exhausted
        _unchanged(self.db, boundary)
        return AdmissionDecision(allowed=allowed)


def record_mcq_result_with_attempt_policy(
    db: Session, payload: MCQResultCommand
) -> ResultWrite:
    """Delegate to the result writer and its required consequences."""
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    result = results.record_mcq_result(
        db,
        payload,
        policy=BoundAttemptPolicy(
            db, payload.tenant_id, payload.person_id, payload.activity_id
        ),
    )
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return result

from __future__ import annotations

from copy import deepcopy
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from uuid import UUID

from dotmac_kernel.models import Party
from pydantic import JsonValue, TypeAdapter

from . import events, exam_engine
from .attempt_contracts import (

    CloseAttemptCommand,
    OpenAttemptCommand,

)
from .attempt_models import ActivityAttempt
from .event_contracts import EventWrite
from .results import _transaction, _unchanged

_IDS: TypeAdapter[JsonValue] = TypeAdapter(JsonValue)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _Sitter:
    id: UUID


def _fact(row: ActivityAttempt) -> AttemptFact:
    return AttemptFact(
        question_ext_ids=_IDS.validate_python(deepcopy(row.question_ext_ids)),
        **{
            name: getattr(row, name)
            for name in AttemptFact.__dataclass_fields__
            if name != "question_ext_ids"
        },
    )


def _lock_learner(db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID) -> None:
    # Exact source NO KEY UPDATE: compatible with FK KEY SHARE, exclusive admission.
    # A missing row is deliberately ignored; product authorization owns identity.
    db.execute(
        select(Party.id)
        .where(Party.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Party.id == person_id)
        .with_for_update(key_share=True, read=False)
    )


def _open_attempt(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, activity_id: UUID
) -> ActivityAttempt | None:
    return db.scalars(
        select(ActivityAttempt)
        .where(ActivityAttempt.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(ActivityAttempt.activity_id == activity_id)
        .where(ActivityAttempt.person_id == person_id)
        .where(ActivityAttempt.submitted_at.is_(None))
        .order_by(ActivityAttempt.started_at.desc())
    ).first()


def _prior_attempts(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, activity_id: UUID
) -> int:
    return int(
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(ActivityAttempt)
            .where(ActivityAttempt.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(ActivityAttempt.activity_id == activity_id)
            .where(ActivityAttempt.person_id == person_id)
        )
        or 0
    )


def open_or_create_attempt(db: Session, payload: OpenAttemptCommand) -> AttemptWrite:
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    payload = payload.model_copy(deep=True)
    scope = {
        "tenant_id": payload.tenant_id,
        "person_id": payload.person_id,
        "activity_id": payload.activity_id,
    }
    _lock_learner(db, tenant_id=payload.tenant_id, person_id=payload.person_id)
    existing = _open_attempt(db, **scope)
    if existing is not None:
        result = AttemptWrite(_fact(existing))
        _unchanged(db, boundary)
        return result
    k = min(payload.count, len(payload.all_ext_ids))
    if k <= 0:
        chosen: list[str] = []
    else:
        variant = f"attempt{_prior_attempts(db, **scope)}:"
        questions = (
            list(payload.questions)
            if payload.questions is not None
            else [SelectionQuestion(ext_id=ext_id) for ext_id in payload.all_ext_ids]
        )
        drawn = exam_engine.select(
            _Sitter(payload.person_id),
            questions,
            exam_engine.SelectionPolicy(total=k),
            variant=variant,
        )
        chosen = [q.ext_id for q in drawn]
    attempt = ActivityAttempt(
        **scope,
        question_ext_ids=chosen,
        started_at=payload.now or datetime.now(UTC),
    )
    db.add(attempt)
    db.flush()
    emitted = events.emit(
        db,
        EventWrite(
            tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
            person_id=payload.person_id,
            kind="activity_started",
            subject_id=payload.activity_id,
            detail={"attempt": len(chosen)},
        ),
    )
    result = AttemptWrite(_fact(attempt), emitted)
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return result


def close_open_attempt(db: Session, payload: CloseAttemptCommand) -> AttemptFact | None:
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    _lock_learner(db, tenant_id=payload.tenant_id, person_id=payload.person_id)
    attempt = _open_attempt(
        db,
        tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
        person_id=payload.person_id,
        activity_id=payload.activity_id,
    )
    if attempt is None:
        _unchanged(db, boundary)
        return None
    attempt.submitted_at = payload.now or datetime.now(UTC)
    db.flush()
    result = _fact(attempt)
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return result


__all__ = ["open_or_create_attempt", "close_open_attempt"]

"""Explicit ERP roster classification, without employment or email-domain guesses.

ERP owns employee references. Matching keys use source strip/lower semantics;
reference bytes are preserved. Existing unmatched classifications remain intact
unless the caller explicitly asserts that the supplied roster is complete.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from dotmac_kernel.models import Party, PartyPerson
from sqlalchemy import Select, func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .participation_contracts import (
    AudienceCounts,
    ClassificationCounts,
    ClassifyRosterCommand,
    UnclassifiedPerson,
)
from .participation_models import Enrollment
from .results import _transaction, _unchanged

STAFF = "staff"
EXTERNAL = "external"
AUDIENCES = (STAFF, EXTERNAL)


def active_student_person_ids_select(
    *, tenant_id: UUID, cohort_id: UUID | None = None
) -> Select[tuple[UUID]]:
    """Build a distinct enrollment relation for caller-owned SQL composition.

    Construction does not execute SQL. Account/authentication eligibility and
    the caller Session's execution and autoflush remain with the consumer.
    """
    stmt = (
        select(Enrollment.person_id)
        .where(
            Enrollment.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            Enrollment.status == "active",
            Enrollment.role_in_cohort == "student",
        )
        .distinct()
    )
    if cohort_id is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(Enrollment.cohort_id == cohort_id)
    return stmt


def classify_from_roster(
    db: Session, command: ClassifyRosterCommand
) -> ClassificationCounts:
    """Mutate active student rows and flush inside the caller's transaction.

    Falsey email/reference entries are discarded; the last colliding normalized
    key wins. Source queries may autoflush pending caller writes and errors are
    propagated for caller rollback. No savepoint or atomic-refusal promise.
    """
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    normalized = {
        (email or "").strip().lower(): ref
        for email, ref in command.roster.items()
        if email and ref
    }
    staff = external = unclassified_count = unchanged = 0
    rows = db.execute(
        select(Enrollment, Party.email)
        .join(
            Party,
            (Party.id == Enrollment.person_id)
            & (Party.tenant_id == Enrollment.tenant_id),
        )
        .join(PartyPerson, PartyPerson.party_id == Party.id)
        .where(
            Enrollment.tenant_id == command.tenant_id,
            Enrollment.status == "active",
            Enrollment.role_in_cohort == "student",
        )
    ).all()
    for row, email in rows:
        ref = normalized.get((email or "").strip().lower())
        if ref is not None:
            if row.audience == STAFF and row.employee_ref == ref:
                unchanged += 1
                continue
            row.audience = STAFF
            row.employee_ref = ref
            staff += 1
        elif command.mark_rest_external:
            if row.audience == EXTERNAL:
                unchanged += 1
                continue
            row.audience = EXTERNAL
            row.employee_ref = None
            external += 1
        else:
            unclassified_count += 1
    db.flush()
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return ClassificationCounts(staff, external, unclassified_count, unchanged)


def unclassified(db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID) -> tuple[UnclassifiedPerson, ...]:
    """Distinct email/first/last source rows in email order, with source names."""
    rows = db.execute(
        select(Party.email, PartyPerson.first_name, PartyPerson.last_name)
        .select_from(Party)
        .join(PartyPerson, PartyPerson.party_id == Party.id)
        .join(
            Enrollment,
            (Enrollment.person_id == Party.id)
            & (Enrollment.tenant_id == Party.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(
            Enrollment.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            Enrollment.status == "active",
            Enrollment.role_in_cohort == "student",
            Enrollment.audience.is_(None),
        )
        .distinct()
        .order_by(Party.email)
    ).all()
    return tuple(
        UnclassifiedPerson(email, f"{first or ''} {last or ''}".strip())
        for email, first, last in rows
    )


def counts_by_audience(db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID) -> AudienceCounts:
    """Count distinct people per audience, including people in several groups."""
    counts = {STAFF: 0, EXTERNAL: 0, "unclassified": 0}
    for value, count in db.execute(
        select(Enrollment.audience, func.count(func.distinct(Enrollment.person_id)))
        .where(
            Enrollment.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            Enrollment.status == "active",
            Enrollment.role_in_cohort == "student",
        )
        .group_by(Enrollment.audience)
    ).all():
        counts[value or "unclassified"] = int(count)
    return AudienceCounts(counts[STAFF], counts[EXTERNAL], counts["unclassified"])


def staff_person_ids(db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID) -> tuple[UUID, ...]:
    return tuple(
        db.scalars(
            select(Enrollment.person_id)
            .where(
                Enrollment.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                Enrollment.status == "active",
                Enrollment.role_in_cohort == "student",
                Enrollment.audience == STAFF,
            )
            .distinct()
        ).all()
    )

Parsing, lint-before-course lookup, messages and transaction outcome remain
product-owned. Reuse the curriculum loader's original Session and flushes;
leave final Activity changes staged with the source's raw policy values.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from sqlalchemy import select

from .bank_activity_contracts import (
    BankActivityImportResult,
    ImportBankWithActivityCommand,
)
from .curriculum import load_bank
from .models import Activity, Course


def import_bank_with_activity(
    db: Session, command: ImportBankWithActivityCommand
) -> BankActivityImportResult | None:
    """Skip an absent tenant course; otherwise load its bank and stage Activity."""
    doc = command.doc
    course = db.scalars(
        select(Course).where(
            Course.tenant_id == command.tenant_id, Course.slug == doc.course
        )
    ).first()
    if course is None:
        return None

    bank = load_bank(db, tenant_id=command.tenant_id, course_id=course.id, doc=doc)
    pass_threshold = doc.policy.get(
        "pass_threshold",
        {"chapter": 0.0, "mid": 0.60, "final": 0.70}.get(doc.kind, 0.0),
    )
    title = (
        f"Chapter {doc.chapter} test"
        if doc.kind == "chapter"
        else f"{doc.kind.title()} assessment"
    )
    activity = db.scalars(
        select(Activity).where(
            Activity.tenant_id == command.tenant_id,
            Activity.course_id == course.id,
            Activity.bank_id == bank.id,
        )
    ).first()
    created = activity is None
    if activity is None:
        activity = Activity(
            tenant_id=command.tenant_id,
            course_id=course.id,
            chapter_number=doc.chapter,
            type="mcq_test",
            bank_id=bank.id,
            title=title,
            pass_threshold=pass_threshold,
        )
        db.add(activity)
    else:
        for column, value in (("title", title), ("pass_threshold", pass_threshold)):
            setattr(activity, column, value)

    applied_policy: list[tuple[str, object]] = []
    for key, column in (
        ("pool", "question_count"),
        ("max_attempts", "max_attempts"),
        ("mode", "assessment_mode"),
    ):
        if key in doc.policy:
            setattr(activity, column, doc.policy[key])
            applied_policy.append((key, doc.policy[key]))

    return BankActivityImportResult(
        bank_id=bank.id,
        title=title,
        created=created,
        applied_policy=tuple(applied_policy),
    )

"""Certificate record issuance; presentation and delivery stay with products."""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from uuid import uuid4

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .completion import lock_existing_completion
from .event_contracts import EventWrite
from .events import emit
from .models import Certificate
from .progress_contracts import CertificateCommand, CertificateFact, CertificateIssue


class CertificateNotEligible(ValueError):
    """The course has no completed aggregate and no issued certificate."""


def _serial() -> str:
    return f"CERT-{uuid4().hex[:12].upper()}"


def _fact(cert: Certificate) -> CertificateFact:
    return CertificateFact(
        id=cert.id,
        tenant_id=cert.tenant_id,
        person_id=cert.person_id,
        course_id=cert.course_id,
        serial=cert.serial,
        issued_at=cert.issued_at,
        created_at=cert.created_at,
        updated_at=cert.updated_at,
    )


def issue_certificate(db: Session, payload: CertificateCommand) -> CertificateIssue:
    if not db.in_transaction():
        raise ValueError("certificate issuance requires a caller transaction")
    query = select(Certificate).where(
        Certificate.tenant_id == payload.tenant_id,
        Certificate.person_id == payload.person_id,
        Certificate.course_id == payload.course_id,
    )
    existing = db.scalars(query).first()
    if existing is not None:
        return CertificateIssue(certificate=_fact(existing), created=False)
    completion = lock_existing_completion(
        db,
        tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
        person_id=payload.person_id,
        course_id=payload.course_id,
    )
    # Lock wait may have allowed the first issuer to commit its certificate.
    existing = db.scalars(query).first()
    if existing is not None:
        return CertificateIssue(certificate=_fact(existing), created=False)
    if completion is None or completion.status != "completed":
        raise CertificateNotEligible(
            "course not completed; certificate cannot be issued"
        )
    cert = Certificate(
        tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
        person_id=payload.person_id,
        course_id=payload.course_id,
        serial=_serial(),
        issued_at=payload.now or datetime.now(UTC),
    )
    db.add(cert)
    # Required consequence: never hide insertion/flush failure in a savepoint.
    db.flush()
    event = emit(
        db,
        EventWrite(
            tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
            person_id=payload.person_id,
            kind="certificate_earned",
            course_id=payload.course_id,
            subject_id=payload.course_id,
            detail={"serial": cert.serial},
        ),
    )
    return CertificateIssue(certificate=_fact(cert), created=True, event=event)

def _locked_query(
    *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, course_id: UUID
) -> Select[tuple[CourseCompletion]]:
    return (
        select(CourseCompletion)
        .where(
            CourseCompletion.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            CourseCompletion.person_id == person_id,
            CourseCompletion.course_id == course_id,
        )
        .with_for_update()
        .execution_options(populate_existing=True)
    )


def lock_existing_completion(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, course_id: UUID
) -> CourseCompletion | None:
    return db.scalars(
        _locked_query(tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, course_id=course_id)
    ).first()


def ensure_locked_completion(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, course_id: UUID
) -> CourseCompletion:
    db.execute(
        insert(CourseCompletion)
        .values(
            id=uuid4(),
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            person_id=person_id,
            course_id=course_id,
            pct=0.0,
            status="in_progress",
        )
        .on_conflict_do_nothing(
            index_elements=[
                CourseCompletion.tenant_id,
                CourseCompletion.person_id,
                CourseCompletion.course_id,
            ]
        )
    )
    return db.scalars(
        _locked_query(tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, course_id=course_id)
    ).one()


def recompute_completion(db: Session, payload: CompletionCommand) -> CompletionResult:
    """Flush required progress/certificate writes in the supplied transaction.

    Supported concurrency uses READ COMMITTED, as in the source service.
    A lock wait does not refresh a preexisting REPEATABLE READ snapshot.
    """
    if not db.in_transaction():
        raise ValueError("completion requires a caller transaction")
    rec = ensure_locked_completion(
        db,
        tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
        person_id=payload.person_id,
        course_id=payload.course_id,
    )
    total = (
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(Activity)
            .where(
                Activity.tenant_id == payload.tenant_id,
                Activity.course_id == payload.course_id,
            )
        )
        or 0
    )
    best = best_scores_for(
        db,
        tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
        person_id=payload.person_id,
        course_id=payload.course_id,
    )
    passed = sum(1 for score in best.values() if score.passed)
    is_complete = total > 0 and passed == total
    first_completion = is_complete and rec.completed_at is None
    rec.pct = passed / total if total else 0.0
    if is_complete:
        rec.status = "completed"
        if rec.completed_at is None:
            rec.completed_at = payload.now or datetime.now(UTC)
    else:
        rec.status = "in_progress"
        rec.completed_at = None
    db.flush()
    certificate = None
    if first_completion:
        from .certificates import issue_certificate

        certificate = issue_certificate(
            db,
            CertificateCommand(
                tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
                person_id=payload.person_id,
                course_id=payload.course_id,
                now=payload.now,
            ),
        )
    return CompletionResult(
        completion=CompletionFact(
            id=rec.id,
            tenant_id=rec.tenant_id,
            person_id=rec.person_id,
            course_id=rec.course_id,
            status=rec.status,
            pct=rec.pct,
            completed_at=rec.completed_at,
            created_at=rec.created_at,
            updated_at=rec.updated_at,
        ),
        first_completion=first_completion,
        certificate=certificate,
    )


def get_completion(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, course_id: UUID
) -> CompletionFact | None:
    """Read the stored aggregate without locking, recomputing or issuing.

    This is not a visibility or certificate-eligibility decision. The supplied
    Session retains its normal query/autoflush behavior and caller ownership.
    """
    row = db.scalars(
        select(CourseCompletion).where(
            CourseCompletion.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            CourseCompletion.person_id == person_id,
            CourseCompletion.course_id == course_id,
        )
    ).first()
    if row is None:
        return None
    return CompletionFact(
        id=row.id,
        tenant_id=row.tenant_id,
        person_id=row.person_id,
        course_id=row.course_id,
        status=row.status,
        pct=row.pct,
        completed_at=row.completed_at,
        created_at=row.created_at,
        updated_at=row.updated_at,
    )

"""Reusable curriculum lifecycle from Academy 0968881.

Caller supplies an active Session/root transaction and normalized rendered
content, or a trusted product renderer. Commands mutate and flush only. Source read-then-write concurrency
and database uniqueness behavior are preserved; no retry guarantee is added.
"""

class CurriculumConflict(ValueError):
    pass


class CurriculumNotFound(ValueError):
    pass


def _fact(row: Chapter) -> ChapterFact:
    return ChapterFact(
        **{name: getattr(row, name) for name in ChapterFact.__dataclass_fields__}
    )


def _bank_fact(row: QuestionBank) -> BankFact:
    return BankFact(
        **{name: getattr(row, name) for name in BankFact.__dataclass_fields__}
    )


def _course(db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, course_id: UUID) -> Course:
    row = db.scalars(
        select(Course).where(Course.tenant_id == tenant_id, Course.id == course_id)
    ).first()
    if row is None:
        raise CurriculumNotFound("course not found for tenant")
    return row


def _course_fact(db: Session, row: Course) -> CourseFact:
    result = get_course(db, tenant_id=row.tenant_id, course_id=row.id)
    if result is None:
        raise AssertionError
    return result


def create_course(db: Session, command: CourseCreate) -> CourseFact:
    """Normalize slug and reject an observed duplicate; create an in-app draft."""
    from uuid import uuid4

    boundary = _transaction(db)
    slug = (command.slug or "").strip().lower()
    existing = db.scalars(
        select(Course).where(Course.tenant_id == command.tenant_id, Course.slug == slug)
    ).first()
    if existing is not None:
        raise CurriculumConflict(f"a course with slug {slug!r} already exists")
    result = create_reference_course(
        db,
        CourseWrite(
            id=uuid4(),
            tenant_id=command.tenant_id,
            slug=slug,
            title=command.title,
            discipline=command.discipline,
            source_ref="in-app",
            version=1,
            status="draft",
        ),
    )
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return result


def author_chapter(
    db: Session,
    command: AuthorChapterCommand,
    *,
    render_markdown: Callable[[str], str],
) -> ChapterFact:
    """Resolve the scoped course, then render once before looking up the chapter.

    The trusted product renderer owns HTML safety and must preserve the caller's
    transaction boundary. Renderer failures propagate before chapter work.
    """
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    course = _course(db, command.tenant_id, command.course_id)
    body_html = render_markdown(command.body_md)
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    result = _write_chapter(
        db, course, ChapterWrite(**command.model_dump(), body_html=body_html)
    )
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return result


def upsert_chapter(db: Session, command: ChapterWrite) -> ChapterFact:
    """Every authoring save bumps version, including an identical save."""
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    course = _course(db, command.tenant_id, command.course_id)
    result = _write_chapter(db, course, command)
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return result


def _write_chapter(db: Session, course: Course, command: ChapterWrite) -> ChapterFact:
    chapter = db.scalars(
        select(Chapter).where(
            Chapter.tenant_id == command.tenant_id,
            Chapter.course_id == command.course_id,
            Chapter.number == command.number,
        )
    ).first()
    if chapter is None:
        chapter = Chapter(**command.model_dump(), order_index=command.number)
        db.add(chapter)
    else:
        for name in ("title", "part", "body_md", "body_html"):
            setattr(chapter, name, getattr(command, name))
    course.version += 1
    db.flush()
    result = _fact(chapter)
    return result


def delete_chapter(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, course_id: UUID, chapter_id: UUID
) -> None:
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    course = _course(db, tenant_id, course_id)
    chapter = db.scalars(
        select(Chapter).where(
            Chapter.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            Chapter.course_id == course_id,
            Chapter.id == chapter_id,
        )
    ).first()
    if chapter is None:
        raise CurriculumNotFound("chapter not found for tenant")
    db.delete(chapter)
    course.version += 1
    db.flush()
    _unchanged(db, boundary)


def chapter_source_hash(source: ChapterSource) -> str:
    """Exact source hash: raw UTF-8 plus hex fingerprint of sorted figure IDs."""
    figures = hashlib.sha256()
    for figure in sorted(source.figures, key=lambda item: item.id):
        figures.update(figure.id.encode())
        figures.update(figure.content if figure.content is not None else b"<missing>")
    return hashlib.sha256(source.raw_utf8 + figures.hexdigest().encode()).hexdigest()


def import_manual(db: Session, command: ManualImport) -> CourseFact:
    """Upsert metadata and hash-changed chapters; absent chapters are retained.

    A new course with chapters starts at version 2, exactly as the source.
    Existing body_md/order_index survive an imported-content update.
    """
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    course = db.scalars(
        select(Course).where(
            Course.tenant_id == command.tenant_id, Course.slug == command.slug
        )
    ).first()
    if course is None:
        course = Course(
            tenant_id=command.tenant_id,
            slug=command.slug,
            title=command.title,
            discipline=command.discipline,
            source_ref=command.source_ref,
            version=1,
        )
        db.add(course)
        db.flush()
    changed = False
    for name in ("title", "discipline", "source_ref"):
        if getattr(course, name) != getattr(command, name):
            setattr(course, name, getattr(command, name))
            changed = True
    for doc in command.chapters:
        existing = db.scalars(
            select(Chapter).where(
                Chapter.tenant_id == command.tenant_id,
                Chapter.course_id == course.id,
                Chapter.number == doc.number,
            )
        ).first()
        if existing is None:
            db.add(
                Chapter(
                    tenant_id=command.tenant_id,
                    course_id=course.id,
                    **doc.model_dump(),
                    order_index=doc.number,
                )
            )
            changed = True
        elif existing.source_hash != doc.source_hash:
            for name in ("title", "part", "body_html", "source_hash"):
                setattr(existing, name, getattr(doc, name))
            changed = True
    if changed:
        course.version += 1
    db.flush()
    result = _course_fact(db, course)
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return result


def public_catalog(db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID) -> tuple[PublicCatalogItem, ...]:
    """Anonymous catalog eligibility is published AND listed, ordered by title."""
    rows = db.execute(
        select(Course, func.count(Chapter.id))
        .outerjoin(
            Chapter,
            (Chapter.tenant_id == Course.tenant_id) & (Chapter.course_id == Course.id),
        )
        .where(
            Course.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            Course.status == "published",
            Course.listed.is_(True),
        )
        .group_by(Course.id)
        .order_by(Course.title)
    ).all()
    return tuple(
        PublicCatalogItem(
            course=CourseFact(
                **{
                    name: getattr(course, name)
                    for name in CourseFact.__dataclass_fields__
                }
            ),
            chapter_count=int(count),
        )
        for course, count in rows
    )


def lint_bank(doc: BankDoc | BankDocument) -> list[str]:
    """Delegate to the ported single pure rules owner; loading does not lint."""
    if isinstance(doc, BankDoc):
        return _lint_bank(doc)
    return _lint_bank(
        BankDoc(
            course=doc.course,
            chapter=doc.chapter,
            kind=doc.kind,
            version=doc.version,
            questions=[q.model_dump() for q in doc.questions],
            policy=dict(doc.policy),
        )
    )


def load_bank(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, course_id: UUID, doc: BankDoc | BankDocument
) -> BankFact:
    """Replace questions in source order, preserving raw decoder failure stages.

    BankDoc is deliberately unvalidated: defaults, category conversion and weight
    conversion happen per question, after bank creation or replacement deletion.
    """
    boundary = _transaction(db)
    bank = db.scalars(
        select(QuestionBank).where(
            QuestionBank.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            QuestionBank.course_id == course_id,
            QuestionBank.chapter_number == doc.chapter,
            QuestionBank.kind == doc.kind,
        )
    ).first()
    if bank is None:
        bank = QuestionBank(
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            course_id=course_id,
            chapter_number=doc.chapter,
            kind=doc.kind,
            version=doc.version,
        )
        db.add(bank)
        db.flush()
    else:
        db.execute(delete(Question).where(Question.bank_id == bank.id))
        bank.version = doc.version
    for question in doc.questions:
        values = (
            cast(dict[str, Any], question)
            if isinstance(doc, BankDoc)
            else cast(BankQuestion, question).model_dump()
        )
        db.add(
            Question(
                tenant_id=tenant_id,
                bank_id=bank.id,
                ext_id=values["id"],
                stem=values["stem"],
                type=values["type"],
                options=values.get("options", []),
                correct=values.get("correct", []),
                rubric_category=values["rubric_category"],
                category=_competency_of(values),
                explanation=values.get("explanation", ""),
                weight=int(values.get("weight", 1)),
            )
        )
    db.flush()
    result = _bank_fact(bank)
    _unchanged(db, boundary)
    return result


def doc_from_db(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, bank_id: UUID, course_slug: str
) -> BankDocument:
    bank = db.scalars(
        select(QuestionBank).where(
            QuestionBank.tenant_id == tenant_id, QuestionBank.id == bank_id
        )
    ).first()
    if bank is None:
        raise CurriculumNotFound("bank not found for tenant")
    rows = db.scalars(
        select(Question)
        .where(Question.tenant_id == tenant_id, Question.bank_id == bank.id)
        .order_by(Question.ext_id)
    ).all()
    return BankDocument(
        course=course_slug,
        chapter=bank.chapter_number,
        kind=bank.kind,
        version=bank.version,
        questions=tuple(
            BankQuestion(
                id=q.ext_id,
                stem=q.stem,
                type=q.type,
                options=q.options,
                correct=q.correct,
                rubric_category=q.rubric_category,
                category=q.category,
                explanation=q.explanation,
                weight=q.weight,
            )
            for q in rows
        ),
        policy={},
    )


def decoded_doc_from_db(
    db: Session, *, bank: BankDocumentHeader, course_slug: str
) -> BankDoc:
    """Rebuild a BankDoc from a bank already in the database.

    So the live estate can be checked with :func:`lint_bank` itself rather than
    a second implementation of the rules in SQL. Two implementations of the same
    decision drift the moment a threshold moves; this keeps one.
    """
    rows = db.scalars(
        select(Question)
        .where(Question.tenant_id == bank.tenant_id)
        .where(Question.bank_id == bank.id)
        .order_by(Question.ext_id)
    ).all()
    return BankDoc(
        course=course_slug,
        chapter=bank.chapter_number,
        kind=bank.kind,
        version=bank.version,
        questions=[
            {
                "id": q.ext_id,
                "stem": q.stem,
                "type": q.type,
                "options": q.options,
                "correct": q.correct,
                "rubric_category": q.rubric_category,
                "category": q.category,
                "explanation": q.explanation,
                "weight": q.weight,
            }
            for q in rows
        ],
        # Policy lives on the Activity once loaded, not on the bank, so a
        # database-sourced doc carries none — and lint_bank skips an empty one.
        policy={},
    )

"""Product-neutral normalized input and immutable curriculum facts.

File decoding, title presentation, figure discovery, YAML and safe rendering
are adapter responsibilities. No command chooses a transaction outcome.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol
from uuid import UUID

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, JsonValue

from .references import CourseFact


class CurriculumInput(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


class CourseCreate(CurriculumInput):
    tenant_id: UUID
    slug: str
    title: str
    discipline: str


class AuthorChapterCommand(CurriculumInput):
    """Editable source; HTML is supplied by the trusted product renderer."""

    tenant_id: UUID
    course_id: UUID
    number: int
    title: str
    body_md: str
    part: str = ""


class ChapterWrite(CurriculumInput):
    tenant_id: UUID
    course_id: UUID
    number: int
    title: str
    body_md: str
    # Already rendered and sanitized by the caller's trusted renderer.
    body_html: str
    part: str = ""


class FigureSource(CurriculumInput):
    id: str
    content: bytes | None


class ChapterSource(CurriculumInput):
    # Exact raw.encode('utf-8') supplied by the Academy read_text adapter;
    # never normalized markdown, metadata or rendered HTML.
    raw_utf8: bytes
    # The adapter supplies one entry per distinct referenced figure ID.
    figures: tuple[FigureSource, ...] = ()


class ImportedChapter(CurriculumInput):
    number: int
    title: str
    part: str = ""
    body_html: str
    source_hash: str


class ManualImport(CurriculumInput):
    tenant_id: UUID
    slug: str
    # Adapter supplies learner-facing display title (product prefix removed).
    title: str
    discipline: str
    source_ref: str
    # Preserve source sorted-file encounter order, including repeated numbers.
    chapters: tuple[ImportedChapter, ...] = ()


class BankQuestion(CurriculumInput):
    id: str
    stem: str
    type: str
    rubric_category: str
    options: JsonValue = Field(default_factory=list)
    # Numeric questions carry a scalar; preserve source JSON shape.
    correct: JsonValue = Field(default_factory=list)
    category: JsonValue = None
    competency: JsonValue = None
    explanation: str = ""
    weight: int = 1


class BankDocument(CurriculumInput):
    course: str
    chapter: int | None = None
    kind: str
    version: int = 1
    questions: tuple[BankQuestion, ...]
    # Raw declared keys are retained for the original linter's diagnostics.
    policy: dict[str, JsonValue] = Field(default_factory=dict)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ChapterFact:
    id: UUID
    tenant_id: UUID
    course_id: UUID
    number: int
    title: str
    part: str
    body_md: str
    body_html: str
    source_hash: str
    order_index: int


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BankFact:
    id: UUID
    tenant_id: UUID
    course_id: UUID
    chapter_number: int | None
    kind: str
    version: int


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class PublicCatalogItem:
    course: CourseFact
    chapter_count: int


class BankDocumentHeader(Protocol):
    """Trusted, already supplied bank metadata for a source-faithful raw read."""

    @property
    def tenant_id(self) -> UUID: ...

    @property
    def id(self) -> UUID: ...

    @property
    def chapter_number(self) -> int | None: ...

    @property
    def kind(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def version(self) -> int: ...

"""Curriculum and reading records from Academy 0968881.

References retain the source's individual contracts: bank course references
and reading person IDs are logical UUIDs; read/annotation chapter references
are simple ID FKs, not tenant composite constraints.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from uuid import UUID

from dotmac_kernel.models import Base as KernelBase
from dotmac_kernel.models import Tenant, TimestampMixin, uuid_pk
from dotmac_kernel.namespaces import schema_table_args
from sqlalchemy import (
    JSON,
    ForeignKey,
    ForeignKeyConstraint,
    Integer,
    String,
    Text,
    UniqueConstraint,
)
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import JSONB
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import UUID as PG_UUID
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from .models import SCHEMA


class Chapter(KernelBase, TimestampMixin):
    __tablename__ = "chapters"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id", "course_id", "number", name="uq_chapters_tenant_course_number"
        ),
        ForeignKeyConstraint(
            ["tenant_id", "course_id"],
            [f"{SCHEMA}.courses.tenant_id", f"{SCHEMA}.courses.id"],
            ondelete="CASCADE",
            name="fk_chapters_tenant_course",
        ),
        schema_table_args(SCHEMA),
    )
    id: Mapped[UUID] = uuid_pk()
    tenant_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PG_UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey(Tenant.__table__.c.id, ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )
    course_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PG_UUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=False, index=True
    )
    number: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(200), nullable=False)
    part: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), nullable=False, default="")
    body_html: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False, default="")
    # Editable markdown source for in-app authoring (Slice 5/#8); body_html is the
    # rendered output. Empty for filesystem-imported chapters.
    body_md: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False, default="")
    source_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(64), nullable=False, default="")
    order_index: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False, default=0)


class QuestionBank(KernelBase, TimestampMixin):
    __tablename__ = "question_banks"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_question_banks_tenant_id_id"),
        schema_table_args(SCHEMA),
    )
    id: Mapped[UUID] = uuid_pk()
    tenant_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PG_UUID(as_uuid=True),
        ForeignKey(Tenant.__table__.c.id, ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )
    course_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        PG_UUID(as_uuid=True), nullable=False, index=True
    )
    chapter_number: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(Integer)
    kind: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(10), nullable=False)  # chapter|mid|final
    version: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False, default=1)


class Question(KernelBase, TimestampMixin):
    __tablename__ = "questions"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id", "bank_id", "ext_id", name="uq_questions_bank_ext"
        ),
        ForeignKeyConstraint(
            ["tenant_id", "bank_id"],
            [f"{SCHEMA}.question_banks.tenant_id", f"{SCHEMA}.question_banks.id"],
            ondelete="CASCADE",
            name="fk_questions_tenant_bank",
        ),
        schema_table_args(SCHEMA),

The V1 seven-table protocol and its row contracts remain unchanged. Every new
persisted column is mandatory, including nullable and raw historical content.
This protocol extension is not a distribution version or cutover authorization.

)

    ("chapters", ChapterRowV2),
    ("question_banks", QuestionBankRowV2),

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, repr=False)
class LearningSnapshotV2:
    """All fourteen tables within explicit genuine tenants, including zero-row ones."""

    version: Literal[2]
    tenant_ids: tuple[UUID, ...]
    courses: tuple[CourseRowV1, ...]
    activities: tuple[ActivityRowV1, ...]
    submissions: tuple[SubmissionRowV1, ...]
    scores: tuple[ScoreRowV1, ...]
    course_completions: tuple[CourseCompletionRowV1, ...]
    certificates: tuple[CertificateRowV1, ...]
    learning_events: tuple[LearningEventRowV1, ...]
    chapters: tuple[ChapterRowV2, ...]
    question_banks: tuple[QuestionBankRowV2, ...]
    questions: tuple[QuestionRowV2, ...]
    chapter_reads: tuple[ChapterReadRowV2, ...]
    subtopic_reads: tuple[SubtopicReadRowV2, ...]
    chapter_bookmarks: tuple[ChapterBookmarkRowV2, ...]
    chapter_notes: tuple[ChapterNoteRowV2, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if type(self.version) is not int or self.version != 2:
            raise SnapshotValidationError("unsupported fourteen-table snapshot version")
        _first_slice(self)  # Existing closed row/extent validation, without writes.
        extent = set(self.tenant_ids)
        for table, row_type in _CURRICULUM_ROW_TYPES:
            rows = getattr(self, table)
            if type(rows) is not tuple:
                raise SnapshotValidationError(f"storage rows must be a tuple: {table}")
            keys: set[UUID] = set()
            for row in rows:
                if type(row) is not row_type:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"wrong storage row contract: {table}"
                    )
                row.__post_init__()
                if row.tenant_id not in extent:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"storage row outside declared extent: {table}/{row.id}"
                    )
                if row.id in keys:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"duplicate storage key: {table}/{row.id}"
                    )
                keys.add(row.id)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return "LearningSnapshotV2(<fourteen-table storage rows>)"


def _first_slice(snapshot: LearningSnapshotV2) -> LearningSnapshotV1:
    """Internal seven-table projection; it does not verify fourteen-table scope."""
    return LearningSnapshotV1(
        version=1,
        tenant_ids=snapshot.tenant_ids,
        courses=snapshot.courses,
        activities=snapshot.activities,
        submissions=snapshot.submissions,
        scores=snapshot.scores,
        course_completions=snapshot.course_completions,
        certificates=snapshot.certificates,
        learning_events=snapshot.learning_events,
    )


class SnapshotClosureErrorV2(SnapshotValidationError):
    """An actual storage FK lacks its parent; report the child location only."""

    def __init__(self, table: str, key: UUID, column: str) -> None:
        self.table, self.key, self.column = table, key, column
        super().__init__(f"unclosed storage reference: {table}/{key}/{column}")

class VerificationObservationV2:

    version: Literal[2]

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, repr=False)
class LearningSnapshotV5:
    """All twenty-seven tables, with explicit genuinely scoped tenant extent."""

    version: Literal[5]
    tenant_ids: tuple[UUID, ...]
    courses: tuple[_v1.CourseRowV1, ...]
    activities: tuple[_v1.ActivityRowV1, ...]
    submissions: tuple[_v1.SubmissionRowV1, ...]
    scores: tuple[_v1.ScoreRowV1, ...]
    course_completions: tuple[_v1.CourseCompletionRowV1, ...]
    certificates: tuple[_v1.CertificateRowV1, ...]
    learning_events: tuple[_v1.LearningEventRowV1, ...]
    chapters: tuple[_v2.ChapterRowV2, ...]
    question_banks: tuple[_v2.QuestionBankRowV2, ...]
    questions: tuple[_v2.QuestionRowV2, ...]
    chapter_reads: tuple[_v2.ChapterReadRowV2, ...]
    subtopic_reads: tuple[_v2.SubtopicReadRowV2, ...]
    chapter_bookmarks: tuple[_v2.ChapterBookmarkRowV2, ...]
    chapter_notes: tuple[_v2.ChapterNoteRowV2, ...]
    cohorts: tuple[_v3.CohortRowV3, ...]
    enrollments: tuple[_v3.EnrollmentRowV3, ...]
    tracks: tuple[_v3.TrackRowV3, ...]
    track_courses: tuple[_v3.TrackCourseRowV3, ...]
    cohort_tracks: tuple[_v3.CohortTrackRowV3, ...]
    course_offerings: tuple[_v3.CourseOfferingRowV3, ...]
    course_prerequisites: tuple[_v3.CoursePrerequisiteRowV3, ...]
    activity_attempts: tuple[_v4.ActivityAttemptRowV4, ...]
    attempt_grants: tuple[_v4.AttemptGrantRowV4, ...]

    offering_activities: tuple[OfferingActivityRowV5, ...]
    class_sessions: tuple[ClassSessionRowV5, ...]
    announcements: tuple[AnnouncementRowV5, ...]
    success_queue_entries: tuple[SuccessQueueEntryRowV5, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if type(self.version) is not int or self.version != 5:
            raise SnapshotValidationError(
                "unsupported twenty-seven-table snapshot version"
            )
        _assessment_slice(self)
        extent = set(self.tenant_ids)
        for table, row_type in _DELIVERY_ROW_TYPES:
            rows = getattr(self, table)
            if type(rows) is not tuple:
                raise SnapshotValidationError(f"storage rows must be a tuple: {table}")
            keys: set[UUID] = set()
            for row in rows:
                if type(row) is not row_type:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"wrong storage row contract: {table}"
                    )
                row.__post_init__()
                if row.tenant_id not in extent:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"storage row outside declared extent: {table}/{row.id}"
                    )
                if row.id in keys:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"duplicate storage key: {table}/{row.id}"
                    )
                keys.add(row.id)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return "LearningSnapshotV5(<twenty-seven-table storage rows>)"

"""Source digest counters, without account/recipient or delivery ownership.

HR assembly must perform its original credential/session checks BEFORE invoking
staff_learning_window. Reuse audience.staff_person_ids/counts_by_audience for
classification. Independent reads do not qualify a coupled recipient cutover:
a same-Session set is not the original READ COMMITTED statement snapshot.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Sequence
from datetime import datetime
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .digest_contracts import LearnerWindowActivity, StaffLearningWindow
from .models import (
    KIND_CHAPTER_VIEWED,
    CourseCompletion,
    LearningEvent,
    Score,
    Submission,
)


def staff_learning_window(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, staff_ids: Sequence[UUID], since: datetime
) -> StaffLearningWindow:
    """Source active -> ever-active -> completion-row queries, in that order."""
    if not staff_ids:
        return StaffLearningWindow(frozenset(), frozenset(), 0)
    active_ids = frozenset(
        db.scalars(
            select(LearningEvent.person_id)
            .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(LearningEvent.person_id.in_(staff_ids))
            .where(LearningEvent.occurred_at >= since)
            .distinct()
        ).all()
    )
    ever_active_ids = frozenset(
        db.scalars(
            select(LearningEvent.person_id)
            .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(LearningEvent.person_id.in_(staff_ids))
            .distinct()
        ).all()
    )
    completed = int(
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(CourseCompletion)
            .where(CourseCompletion.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(CourseCompletion.person_id.in_(staff_ids))
            .where(CourseCompletion.completed_at >= since)
        )
        or 0
    )
    return StaffLearningWindow(active_ids, ever_active_ids, completed)


def learner_window_activity(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, since: datetime
) -> LearnerWindowActivity:
    """Distinct nonnull chapter subjects, submission rows and passing-score rows."""
    chapters = int(
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count(func.distinct(LearningEvent.subject_id)))
            .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(LearningEvent.person_id == person_id)
            .where(LearningEvent.kind == KIND_CHAPTER_VIEWED)
            .where(LearningEvent.occurred_at >= since)
        )
        or 0
    )
    submissions = int(
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(Submission)
            .where(Submission.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(Submission.person_id == person_id)
            .where(Submission.created_at >= since)
        )
        or 0
    )
    passed = int(
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(Score)
            .join(
                Submission,
                (Submission.id == Score.submission_id)
                & (Submission.tenant_id == Score.tenant_id),
            )
            .where(Score.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(Submission.person_id == person_id)
            .where(Score.created_at >= since)
            .where(Score.passed.is_(True))
        )
        or 0
    )
    return LearnerWindowActivity(chapters, submissions, passed)
