"""Source-derived event append and primitive queries on a supplied Session.

The caller owns the transaction. ``record`` propagates errors; ``emit`` isolates
an optional append in a SAVEPOINT and reports its actual local outcome. Neither
method commits, delivers, or creates a session. Day throttling deliberately keeps
the source's SELECT race; product timezone selection belongs to the adapter.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from copy import deepcopy
from datetime import (
    UTC,
    datetime,
    time,
    timedelta,
    tzinfo,
)
from uuid import UUID

from dotmac_kernel.models import Party, PartyType
from pydantic import JsonValue, TypeAdapter
from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert as pg_insert
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from dotmac_learning.event_contracts import (
    EventEmission,
    EventFact,
    EventWrite,
    WeekBucket,
)
from dotmac_learning.models import (
    EVENT_KINDS,
    KIND_CERTIFICATE_EARNED,
    KIND_CHAPTER_COMPLETED,
    KIND_CHAPTER_VIEWED,
    KIND_COURSE_VIEWED,
    LearningEvent,
)

_ONCE_PER_SUBJECT = (KIND_CHAPTER_COMPLETED, KIND_CERTIFICATE_EARNED)
_ONCE_PER_LOCAL_DAY = (KIND_COURSE_VIEWED, KIND_CHAPTER_VIEWED)
_DETAIL: TypeAdapter[JsonValue] = TypeAdapter(JsonValue)


def _local_day_start_utc(now: datetime, zone: tzinfo) -> datetime:
    local = now.astimezone(zone)
    return datetime.combine(local.date(), time.min, tzinfo=zone).astimezone(UTC)


def _fact(event: LearningEvent) -> EventFact:
    return EventFact(
        id=event.id,
        tenant_id=event.tenant_id,
        person_id=event.person_id,
        kind=event.kind,
        course_id=event.course_id,
        subject_id=event.subject_id,
        detail=deepcopy(_DETAIL.validate_python(event.detail)),
        occurred_at=event.occurred_at,
        created_at=event.created_at,
        updated_at=event.updated_at,
    )


def record(
    db: Session,
    payload: EventWrite,
    *,
    local_day_zone: tzinfo | None = None,
) -> EventFact | None:
    """Append one event, returning None only when a dedupe rule suppresses it.

    The actual tenant-scoped Party must be a person, even if a malformed
    organization has a person profile. The real dual identity FKs remain the
    existence/cascade backstop; this path takes no explicit identity locks.
    """
    if payload.kind not in EVENT_KINDS:
        raise ValueError("unknown learning-event kind")
    if payload.kind in _ONCE_PER_LOCAL_DAY and local_day_zone is None:
        raise ValueError("daily learning events require local_day_zone")
    party_type = db.scalar(
        select(Party.party_type)
        .where(Party.tenant_id == payload.tenant_id)
        .where(Party.id == payload.person_id)
    )
    if party_type != PartyType.person:
        raise ValueError("learning-event identity must be a tenant-scoped person")
    now = payload.occurred_at or datetime.now(UTC)
    if payload.kind in _ONCE_PER_LOCAL_DAY:
        # Already required above: retain a concrete zone at this typed seam.
        if local_day_zone is None:
            raise AssertionError
        dupe = (
            select(LearningEvent.id)
            .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == payload.tenant_id)
            .where(LearningEvent.person_id == payload.person_id)
            .where(LearningEvent.kind == payload.kind)
            .where(LearningEvent.subject_id == payload.subject_id)
            .where(
                LearningEvent.occurred_at >= _local_day_start_utc(now, local_day_zone)
            )
        )
        if db.scalars(dupe.limit(1)).first() is not None:
            return None
    if payload.kind in _ONCE_PER_SUBJECT:
        # Exact 0047 predicate and ordinary PostgreSQL NULL subject semantics.
        stmt = (
            pg_insert(LearningEvent)
            .values(
                tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
                person_id=payload.person_id,
                kind=payload.kind,
                course_id=payload.course_id,
                subject_id=payload.subject_id,
                detail=payload.detail,
                occurred_at=now,
            )
            .on_conflict_do_nothing(
                index_elements=["tenant_id", "person_id", "kind", "subject_id"],
                index_where=LearningEvent.kind.in_(_ONCE_PER_SUBJECT),
            )
            .returning(LearningEvent.id)
        )
        inserted_id = db.execute(stmt).scalar()
        if inserted_id is None:
            return None
        db.flush()
        event = db.get(LearningEvent, inserted_id)
        if event is None:
            raise RuntimeError("appended learning event is unavailable")
        return _fact(event)
    event = LearningEvent(
        tenant_id=payload.tenant_id,
        person_id=payload.person_id,
        kind=payload.kind,
        course_id=payload.course_id,
        subject_id=payload.subject_id,
        detail=payload.detail,
        occurred_at=now,
    )
    db.add(event)
    db.flush()
    return _fact(event)


def emit(
    db: Session,
    payload: EventWrite,
    *,
    local_day_zone: tzinfo | None = None,
) -> EventEmission:
    """Optionally append, catching failures outside SAVEPOINT exit.

    This module explicitly flushes required pending host state before the
    optional failure handler: a host SQL failure propagates and requires caller
    rollback. Only this append's failures are optional and savepoint-isolated.
    This tightens the Academy source wrapper's implicit-preflush behavior;
    Academy adoption must qualify it at the actual producer boundaries.
    """
    db.flush()
    try:
        with db.begin_nested():
            event = record(db, payload, local_day_zone=local_day_zone)
        return (
            EventEmission("recorded", event)
            if event is not None
            else EventEmission("suppressed")
        )
    except Exception:
        return EventEmission("failed")


def last_activity_at(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID
) -> datetime | None:
    return db.scalar(
        select(func.max(LearningEvent.occurred_at))
        .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(LearningEvent.person_id == person_id)
    )


def weekly_buckets(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    weeks: int = 8,
    kinds: tuple[str, ...] | None = None,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> list[WeekBucket]:
    """Source trailing-week date buckets, oldest first (not calendar realignment)."""
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    start = now - timedelta(weeks=weeks)
    q = (
        select(LearningEvent.occurred_at)
        .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(LearningEvent.person_id == person_id)
        .where(LearningEvent.occurred_at >= start)
    )
    if kinds:
        q = q.where(LearningEvent.kind.in_(kinds))
    stamps = list(db.scalars(q).all())
    buckets: list[WeekBucket] = []
    for i in range(weeks):
        w_start = (now - timedelta(weeks=weeks - i)).date()
        w_end = (now - timedelta(weeks=weeks - i - 1)).date()
        count = sum(1 for stamp in stamps if w_start <= stamp.date() < w_end)
        buckets.append(WeekBucket(week_start=w_start, count=count))
    return buckets


def active_person_ids(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_ids: list[UUID],
    since: datetime,
) -> set[UUID]:
    if not person_ids:
        return set()
    rows = db.scalars(
        select(LearningEvent.person_id)
        .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(LearningEvent.person_id.in_(person_ids))
        .where(LearningEvent.occurred_at >= since)
        .distinct()
    ).all()
    return set(rows)


def kind_counts(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    kinds: tuple[str, ...],
    course_ids: list[UUID] | None = None,
    person_ids: list[UUID] | None = None,
    since: datetime | None = None,
) -> dict[UUID | None, dict[str, int]]:
    """Source per-course/kind counts, with the same optional roster semantics."""
    q = (
        select(LearningEvent.course_id, LearningEvent.kind, func.count())
        .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(LearningEvent.kind.in_(kinds))
        .group_by(LearningEvent.course_id, LearningEvent.kind)
    )
    if course_ids:
        q = q.where(LearningEvent.course_id.in_(course_ids))
    if person_ids is not None:
        q = q.where(LearningEvent.person_id.in_(person_ids))
    if since is not None:
        q = q.where(LearningEvent.occurred_at >= since)
    out: dict[UUID | None, dict[str, int]] = {}
    for course_id, kind, count in db.execute(q).all():
        out.setdefault(course_id, {})[kind] = int(count)
    return out

"""The exam engine — one owner for what an exam *is*.

Before this module the answer depended on who was asking. A learner sitting a
course activity and an applicant sitting the entrance exam shared exactly one
function, ``grade_submission``; selection, option order, validity and result
policy were each implemented once, on whichever side happened to need them
first. Two consequences were live defects rather than asymmetries: course
learners saw an identical option order, so "the answer is the third one"
transferred between them, and a course sitting had no validity gate, so a
forty-second final at chance was recorded as a genuine result.

See ``docs/adr/0005-assessment-engine-owns-exam-logic.md``.

What lives here
---------------
The *decisions*: who may sit, which questions they get, in what order they see
them, whether the sitting counts as signal. Grading stays in ``grading`` as a
pure function; this module calls it rather than reimplementing it.

What does not live here
-----------------------
The *facts* — questions, options, answers, competency tags — which belong to
the banks, and persistence, which belongs to the adapters that know whether
they are writing against a ``Person`` or an ``Applicant``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import random
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Protocol, TypeVar

from pydantic import JsonValue

# A sitting near the guessing baseline, or faster than anyone could read the
# paper, is not a weak candidate — it is an ABSENCE OF DATA, and scoring it as
# a genuine low result pollutes whatever ranking or gradebook consumes it.
#
# Both floors are DERIVED from the paper rather than fixed, because both depend
# on it. The old constants encoded "four options" and "30 questions" in their
# comments and then stopped tracking either: once the entrance paper size became
# configurable, a 60-question sitting was still gated at six minutes. A setting
# would not have fixed that — it would only have added a second value to drift.
SECONDS_PER_QUESTION = 12.0  # faster than this is not reading the question
NEAR_CHANCE_MARGIN = 1.33  # the gate sits this far above the paper's own chance

# Fallbacks for callers that cannot supply the paper. They encode the historical
# assumption — 30 four-option questions — and are what those callers already got.
MIN_VALID_FRACTION = 1.0 / 3.0
MIN_DURATION_SECONDS = 6 * 60

INVALID_NEAR_CHANCE = "near_chance"
INVALID_TOO_FAST = "too_fast"


class Sitter(Protocol):
    """Whoever is taking the exam.

    Deliberately narrow: the engine needs an identity to make its per-sitter
    decisions reproducible, and nothing else. A ``Person`` and an ``Applicant``
    both satisfy this, which is the point — the identity split between admitted
    learners and candidates is an admissions concern, not an exam one.
    """

    # A read-only property rather than an attribute, so both a mutable ORM
    # model and a frozen dataclass adapter satisfy it.
    @property
    def id(self) -> object: ...


class Question(Protocol):
    """The shape the engine needs from a question. Banks own the rest."""

    @property
    def ext_id(self) -> str: ...

    @property
    def category(self) -> str | None: ...

    @property
    def options(self) -> JsonValue: ...


QuestionT = TypeVar("QuestionT", bound=Question)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SelectionPolicy:
    """How many questions to draw, and how.

    ``per_category`` draws that many from each competency, so every sitter is
    measured on the same shape and their per-domain profiles stay comparable —
    a flat draw would hand one sitter nine numeracy items and another two.

    ``total`` draws that many across the bank, ignoring competency.

    Both zero means the whole bank, which is the behaviour that existed before
    any pooling and remains the default.
    """

    per_category: int = 0
    total: int = 0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.per_category and self.total:
            raise ValueError("choose per_category or total, not both")


def _rank(sitter: Sitter, salt: str, key: str) -> str:
    """A stable pseudo-random ordering key for (sitter, thing).

    Deterministic so a reload or a resumed sitting reproduces the same paper,
    and so grading can rebuild what was shown without persisting it. Salted so
    that selection order and presentation order are independent — otherwise the
    first questions drawn would also be the ones whose options moved least.
    """
    return hashlib.sha256(f"{sitter.id}:{salt}{key}".encode()).hexdigest()


def select(
    sitter: Sitter,
    questions: list[QuestionT],
    policy: SelectionPolicy,
    variant: str = "",
) -> list[QuestionT]:
    """The questions this sitter gets, in the order they get them.

    ``variant`` distinguishes repeat sittings by the same person. Without it a
    learner's second attempt at a pooled activity would draw the identical
    paper as their first, which removes the only reason to pool a bank that
    allows retakes. The entrance exam is a single sitting and passes nothing.
    """
    if policy.per_category:
        by_category: dict[str, list[QuestionT]] = {}
        for q in questions:
            by_category.setdefault(
                getattr(q, "category", None) or "general", []
            ).append(q)

        chosen: list[QuestionT] = []
        for group in by_category.values():
            if len(group) <= policy.per_category:
                # A category smaller than the draw contributes all of itself
                # rather than vanishing from the profile.
                chosen.extend(group)
                continue
            ranked = sorted(group, key=lambda q: _rank(sitter, variant, q.ext_id))
            chosen.extend(ranked[: policy.per_category])
    elif policy.total:
        ranked = sorted(questions, key=lambda q: _rank(sitter, variant, q.ext_id))
        chosen = ranked[: policy.total]
    else:
        chosen = list(questions)

    # Re-rank the whole paper so it is not grouped by competency, which would
    # telegraph the structure and let sitters compare notes by section.
    chosen.sort(key=lambda q: _rank(sitter, f"{variant}order:", q.ext_id))
    return chosen


def present_options(sitter: Sitter, question: Question) -> list[str]:
    """This question's options in a per-sitter order.

    A fixed order leaks: sitters talk, and "the answer is C" stays true for
    everyone. Deterministic in (sitter, question) so a reload does not move the
    options under autosaved answers. Safe because answers are submitted by
    option TEXT, so grading is order-independent.
    """
    opts = list(getattr(question, "options", None) or [])
    # Deterministic per-sitter option presentation; never generates credentials
    # or secrets.
    rng = random.Random(_rank(sitter, "", question.ext_id))  # noqa: S311
    rng.shuffle(opts)
    return opts


def chance_baseline(questions: Sequence[Question]) -> float:
    """The score guessing would produce on *this* paper.

    Averaged over the questions that actually offer options, so a paper with
    true/false items reports the ~50% it really carries rather than the 25% a
    four-option assumption would claim.
    """
    per_question = []
    for q in questions:
        opts = getattr(q, "options", None)
        if isinstance(opts, list) and len(opts) >= 2:
            per_question.append(1.0 / len(opts))
    if not per_question:
        return MIN_VALID_FRACTION / NEAR_CHANCE_MARGIN
    return sum(per_question) / len(per_question)


def near_chance_floor(questions: Sequence[Question]) -> float:
    """Scores at or below this are indistinguishable from guessing."""
    return chance_baseline(questions) * NEAR_CHANCE_MARGIN


def duration_floor(questions: Sequence[Question]) -> float:
    """The fastest a sitting could plausibly have been read."""
    return len(questions) * SECONDS_PER_QUESTION


def check_validity(
    fraction: float,
    duration_seconds: float | None,
    *,
    questions: Sequence[Question] | None = None,
) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    """Is this sitting real signal, or an absence of data?

    Pass ``questions`` — the paper actually served — and both floors follow from
    it. Without them the historical constants apply, which is what every caller
    got before the floors were derived.
    """
    score_floor = near_chance_floor(questions) if questions else MIN_VALID_FRACTION
    time_floor = duration_floor(questions) if questions else MIN_DURATION_SECONDS

    if fraction <= score_floor + 1e-9:
        return False, INVALID_NEAR_CHANCE
    if duration_seconds is None or duration_seconds < time_floor:
        return False, INVALID_TOO_FAST
    return True, None

def _grade_trend(db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID) -> GradeTrend:
    rows = list(
        db.execute(
            select(Score.fraction, Score.created_at)
            .join(
                Submission,
                (Submission.id == Score.submission_id)
                & (Submission.tenant_id == Score.tenant_id),
            )
            .where(Score.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(Submission.person_id == person_id)
            .order_by(Score.created_at.desc())
            .limit(10)
        ).all()
    )
    fractions = [float(f) for f, _ in reversed(rows)]
    return _trend_from(fractions)


def _trend_from(fractions: Sequence[float]) -> GradeTrend:
    direction: Literal["flat", "up", "down"] = "flat"
    if len(fractions) >= 4:
        half = len(fractions) // 2
        older = sum(fractions[:half]) / half
        newer = sum(fractions[half:]) / (len(fractions) - half)
        if newer - older > 0.05:
            direction = "up"
        elif older - newer > 0.05:
            direction = "down"
    return GradeTrend(tuple(round(100 * f) for f in fractions), direction)


def _discipline_strengths(
    db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID
) -> DisciplineStrengths:
    """Average best-score fraction per course discipline. Competency-level
    areas arrive with roadmap P5; discipline is the honest available grain."""
    course_ids = list(visible_course_ids(db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id))
    per_discipline: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
    if not course_ids:
        return DisciplineStrengths(None, None, ())
    disciplines = {  # noqa: C416 - retain source-shaped row selection
        cid: disc
        for cid, disc in db.execute(
            select(Course.id, Course.discipline)
            .where(Course.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(Course.id.in_(course_ids))
        ).all()
    }
    best_by_course = best_scores_by_course_for_person(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, course_ids=course_ids
    )
    for course_id, best in best_by_course.items():
        discipline = disciplines.get(course_id)
        if discipline is None or not best:
            continue
        avg = sum(float(s.fraction) for s in best.values()) / len(best)
        per_discipline.setdefault(discipline, []).append(avg)
    return _discipline_summary(per_discipline)


def _discipline_summary(
    per_discipline: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
) -> DisciplineStrengths:
    scored = {d: round(100 * sum(v) / len(v)) for d, v in per_discipline.items() if v}
    if not scored:
        return DisciplineStrengths(None, None, ())
    strong = max(scored, key=lambda d: scored[d])
    weak = min(scored, key=lambda d: scored[d])
    return DisciplineStrengths(
        strong,
        weak if weak != strong else None,
        tuple(DisciplineScore(d, pct) for d, pct in scored.items()),
    )


def _current_blocker(
    db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, now: datetime
) -> CurrentBlocker | None:
    """First blocking activity, by explicit rule:

    - overdue: ``OfferingActivity.due_at`` in the past without a passing best
      score;
    - attempts_exhausted: ``max_attempts`` used without a pass.
    """
    course_ids = visible_course_ids(db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id)
    if not course_ids:
        return None
    best_by_activity: dict[UUID, ScoreFact] = {}
    for course_id in course_ids:
        best_by_activity.update(
            best_scores_for(
                db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, course_id=course_id
            )
        )

    # Scope deadlines to the offerings this person is actually enrolled in.
    # Filtering only by Activity.course_id would let another cohort's offering
    # of the same course contribute a due_at that this learner never had.
    overdue_rows = db.execute(
        select(OfferingActivity.due_at, Activity)
        .join(
            Activity,
            (Activity.id == OfferingActivity.activity_id)
            & (Activity.tenant_id == OfferingActivity.tenant_id),
        )
        .join(
            CourseOffering,
            (CourseOffering.id == OfferingActivity.offering_id)
            & (CourseOffering.tenant_id == OfferingActivity.tenant_id),
        )
        .join(
            Enrollment,
            (Enrollment.cohort_id == CourseOffering.cohort_id)
            & (Enrollment.tenant_id == CourseOffering.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(OfferingActivity.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(OfferingActivity.due_at.is_not(None))
        .where(OfferingActivity.due_at < now)
        .where(CourseOffering.status == "active")
        .where(Enrollment.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Enrollment.status == "active")
        .order_by(OfferingActivity.due_at)
    ).all()
    for due_at, activity in overdue_rows:
        score = best_by_activity.get(activity.id)
        if score is None or not score.passed:
            return CurrentBlocker(
                activity.id, activity.title, activity.course_id, "overdue", due_at
            )

    for activity_id, score in best_by_activity.items():
        if score.passed:
            continue
        activity = db.get(Activity, activity_id)
        if activity is None or activity.max_attempts is None:
            continue
        used = attempts_used(
            db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, activity_id=activity_id
        )
        if attempt_policy.for_learner(
            db,
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            person_id=person_id,
            activity=_activity_fact(activity),
            used=used,
        ).exhausted:
            return CurrentBlocker(
                activity_id,
                activity.title,
                activity.course_id,
                "attempts_exhausted",
                None,
            )
    return None


def learner_activity(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> LearnerActivity:
    """The 'My learning activity' projection for the progress page."""
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    weekly = learning_events.weekly_buckets(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, weeks=8, now=now
    )
    velocity = learning_events.weekly_buckets(
        db,
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        person_id=person_id,
        weeks=4,
        kinds=(KIND_CHAPTER_COMPLETED, KIND_WORK_GRADED),
        now=now,
    )
    last_at = learning_events.last_activity_at(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id
    )
    days_since = (now - last_at).days if last_at else None
    blocker = _current_blocker(db, tenant_id, person_id, now)

    return LearnerActivity(
        tuple(weekly),
        max((b.count for b in weekly), default=0),
        round(sum(b.count for b in velocity) / max(len(velocity), 1), 1),
        _grade_trend(db, tenant_id, person_id),
        days_since,
        _discipline_strengths(db, tenant_id, person_id),
        None,
        blocker,
        _recommendation(blocker.reason if blocker is not None else None, days_since),
    )


def _recommendation(
    reason: BlockerReason | None, days_since: int | None
) -> Recommendation:
    if reason is not None:
        return reason
    if days_since is None:
        return "start_first_chapter"
    if days_since >= 7:
        return "resume_after_week"
    return "continue_unfinished"

def cohort_overview(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    cohort_id: UUID,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> CohortOverview:
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    people = _cohort_people(db, tenant_id, cohort_id)
    course_ids = _cohort_course_ids(db, tenant_id, cohort_id)

    active = learning_events.active_person_ids(
        db,
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        person_ids=people,
        since=now - timedelta(days=ACTIVE_WINDOW_DAYS),
    )

    total_activities = 0
    if course_ids:
        total_activities = int(
            db.scalar(
                select(func.count())
                .select_from(Activity)
                .where(Activity.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                .where(Activity.course_id.in_(course_ids))
            )
            or 0
        )

    overdue_activity_ids: set[UUID] = set()
    if course_ids:
        overdue_activity_ids = {
            r[0]
            for r in db.execute(
                select(OfferingActivity.activity_id)
                .join(
                    CourseOffering,
                    (CourseOffering.id == OfferingActivity.offering_id)
                    & (CourseOffering.tenant_id == OfferingActivity.tenant_id),
                )
                .where(OfferingActivity.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                .where(CourseOffering.cohort_id == cohort_id)
                .where(OfferingActivity.due_at.is_not(None))
                .where(OfferingActivity.due_at < now)
            ).all()
        }

    submitted = overdue = not_attempted = 0
    fractions: list[float] = []
    started: set[UUID] = set()
    half: set[UUID] = set()
    for person_id in people:
        best = _person_best(db, tenant_id, person_id, course_ids)
        if best:
            started.add(person_id)
        fractions.extend(float(s.fraction) for s in best.values())
        submitted += len(best)
        if total_activities:
            not_attempted += max(total_activities - len(best), 0)
            passed = sum(1 for s in best.values() if s.passed)
            if passed >= total_activities / 2:
                half.add(person_id)
        overdue += sum(
            1 for aid in overdue_activity_ids if aid not in best or not best[aid].passed
        )

    completed_count = certified_count = 0
    if people and course_ids:
        completed_count = int(
            db.scalar(
                select(func.count(func.distinct(CourseCompletion.person_id)))
                .where(CourseCompletion.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                .where(CourseCompletion.person_id.in_(people))
                .where(CourseCompletion.course_id.in_(course_ids))
                .where(CourseCompletion.status == "completed")
            )
            or 0
        )
        certified_count = int(
            db.scalar(
                select(func.count(func.distinct(Certificate.person_id)))
                .where(Certificate.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                .where(Certificate.person_id.in_(people))
                .where(Certificate.course_id.in_(course_ids))
            )
            or 0
        )

    # Scope lab failures to this cohort's students and courses. Without the
    # person filter an empty course list would fall back to tenant-wide counts.
    lab_failures_raw = (
        learning_events.kind_counts(
            db,
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            kinds=(KIND_LAB_CHECK_FAILED,),
            course_ids=course_ids,
            person_ids=people,
        )
        if course_ids and people
        else {}
    )
    course_titles = (
        {
            c.id: c.title
            for c in db.scalars(
                select(Course)
                .where(Course.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                .where(Course.id.in_(course_ids))
            ).all()
        }
        if course_ids
        else {}
    )
    lab_failures = tuple(
        LabFailures(
            cid,
            course_titles.get(cid) if cid is not None else None,
            counts.get(KIND_LAB_CHECK_FAILED, 0),
        )
        for cid, counts in lab_failures_raw.items()
        if counts.get(KIND_LAB_CHECK_FAILED, 0)
    )

    this_week = 0
    prior_avg = 0.0
    if people:
        this_week = int(
            db.scalar(
                select(func.count())
                .select_from(LearningEvent)
                .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                .where(LearningEvent.person_id.in_(people))
                .where(LearningEvent.occurred_at >= now - timedelta(days=7))
            )
            or 0
        )
        prior = int(
            db.scalar(
                select(func.count())
                .select_from(LearningEvent)
                .where(LearningEvent.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                .where(LearningEvent.person_id.in_(people))
                .where(LearningEvent.occurred_at >= now - timedelta(days=35))
                .where(LearningEvent.occurred_at < now - timedelta(days=7))
            )
            or 0
        )
        prior_avg = prior / 4.0

    return CohortOverview(
        len(people),
        len(active),
        len(people) - len(active),
        ACTIVE_WINDOW_DAYS,
        submitted,
        overdue,
        not_attempted,
        round(100 * sum(fractions) / len(fractions)) if fractions else None,
        CohortFunnel(
            len(people), len(started), len(half), completed_count, certified_count
        ),
        lab_failures,
        this_week,
        round(prior_avg, 1),
    )


def cohorts_comparison(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, now: datetime | None = None
) -> tuple[CohortComparison, ...]:
    """One comparison row per cohort for the reports index."""
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    rows: list[CohortComparison] = []
    for cohort in db.scalars(select(Cohort).where(Cohort.tenant_id == tenant_id)).all():
        people = _cohort_people(db, tenant_id, cohort.id)
        active = learning_events.active_person_ids(
            db,
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            person_ids=people,
            since=now - timedelta(days=ACTIVE_WINDOW_DAYS),
        )
        course_ids = _cohort_course_ids(db, tenant_id, cohort.id)
        completed = 0
        if people and course_ids:
            completed = int(
                db.scalar(
                    select(func.count(func.distinct(CourseCompletion.person_id)))
                    .where(CourseCompletion.tenant_id == tenant_id)
                    .where(CourseCompletion.person_id.in_(people))
                    .where(CourseCompletion.course_id.in_(course_ids))
                    .where(CourseCompletion.status == "completed")
                )
                or 0
            )
        rows.append(
            CohortComparison(
                ReportCohort(
                    **{
                        field: getattr(cohort, field)
                        for field in ReportCohort.__dataclass_fields__
                    }
                ),
                len(people),
                len(active),
                completed,
                round(100 * completed / len(people)) if people else 0,
            )
        )
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: r.cohort.name.lower())
    return tuple(rows)

"""Learner dashboard projections (roadmap P1a).

This service OWNS the learner-facing dashboard, resume, and progress
projections: each course card carries ONE derived state and ONE action, the
resume target is computed server-side from the last meaningful touch (so it
follows the learner across devices), and the progress overview aggregates
grades, attempts, deadlines and certificate eligibility per course. Routes
render these facts; they do not re-derive state.

States (mutually exclusive, in precedence order):
    locked > upcoming > completed > expired > in_progress
``in_progress`` covers not-yet-started courses too — the card's action
(Start vs Resume) is what distinguishes them.

def _entitled_courses(
    db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID
) -> list[tuple[CourseFact, _Offering]]:
    """(course, offering) pairs the person can see, one row per course.

    Visibility is OWNED by entitlements.visible_course_ids — this query only
    attaches the binding offering window to each visible course. When several
    active offerings cover the same course, the one with the earliest end
    (soonest deadline) wins.
    """
    allowed = visible_course_ids(db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id)
    if not allowed:
        return []
    rows = db.execute(
        select(Course, CourseOffering, Enrollment.access_ends_at)
        .join(
            CourseOffering,
            (CourseOffering.course_id == Course.id)
            & (CourseOffering.tenant_id == Course.tenant_id),
        )
        .join(
            Enrollment,
            (Enrollment.cohort_id == CourseOffering.cohort_id)
            & (Enrollment.tenant_id == CourseOffering.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(Course.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Course.id.in_(allowed))
        .where(CourseOffering.status == "active")
        .where(Enrollment.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Enrollment.status == "active")
        .order_by(Course.title)
    ).all()
    chosen: dict[UUID, tuple[CourseFact, _Offering]] = {}
    for course, offering, access_ends_at in rows:
        effective_end = (
            access_ends_at
            if access_ends_at is not None
            and (offering.ends_at is None or access_ends_at > offering.ends_at)
            else offering.ends_at
        )
        fact = _Offering(
            offering.id,
            offering.cohort_id,
            offering.starts_at,
            offering.ends_at,
            effective_end,
        )
        held = chosen.get(course.id)
        if held is None:
            chosen[course.id] = (_course_fact(course), fact)
            continue
        held_end = held[1].effective_ends_at
        if effective_end is not None and (held_end is None or effective_end < held_end):
            chosen[course.id] = (_course_fact(course), fact)
    return sorted(chosen.values(), key=lambda pair: pair[0].title)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Batched primitives — each computes across ALL of the person's courses in a
# bounded number of queries, so the dashboard/progress render cost does not
# scale with the number of enrolled courses (roadmap review item 5).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _activities_by_course(
    db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, course_ids: Sequence[UUID]
) -> dict[UUID, list[ActivityFact]]:
    if not course_ids:
        return {}
    acts = db.scalars(
        select(Activity)
        .where(Activity.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Activity.course_id.in_(course_ids))
        .order_by(Activity.chapter_number, Activity.type)
    ).all()
    out: dict[UUID, list[ActivityFact]] = {}
    for a in acts:
        out.setdefault(a.course_id, []).append(_activity_fact(a))
    return out


def _chapters_by_course(
    db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, course_ids: Sequence[UUID]
) -> dict[UUID, list[ChapterFact]]:
    if not course_ids:
        return {}
    chs = db.scalars(
        select(Chapter)
        .where(Chapter.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Chapter.course_id.in_(course_ids))
        .order_by(Chapter.number)
    ).all()
    out: dict[UUID, list[ChapterFact]] = {}
    for c in chs:
        out.setdefault(c.course_id, []).append(_chapter_fact(c))
    return out


def _touch_bundle(
    db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, course_ids: Sequence[UUID]
) -> _TouchBundle:
    """Per-course last-touch + last-read + read chapter numbers, in 3 queries.

    Returns {"last_touch": {course_id: (when, chapter_number)},
             "last_read": {course_id: (number, title)},
             "read_numbers": {course_id: set[int]}}.
    'when' is the max across chapter reads, submissions, and opened attempts.
    """
    last_touch: dict[UUID, tuple[datetime, int]] = {}
    last_read: dict[UUID, tuple[int, str]] = {}
    read_numbers: dict[UUID, set[int]] = {}
    if not course_ids:
        return {"last_touch": {}, "last_read": {}, "read_numbers": {}}

    def _offer(course_id: UUID, when: datetime, chapter_number: int | None) -> None:
        if chapter_number is None:
            return
        held = last_touch.get(course_id)
        if held is None or when > held[0]:
            last_touch[course_id] = (when, chapter_number)

    reads = db.execute(
        select(Chapter.course_id, ChapterRead.created_at, Chapter.number, Chapter.title)
        .join(Chapter, Chapter.id == ChapterRead.chapter_id)
        .where(ChapterRead.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(ChapterRead.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Chapter.course_id.in_(course_ids))
        .order_by(ChapterRead.created_at.desc())
    ).all()
    for course_id, when, number, title in reads:
        read_numbers.setdefault(course_id, set()).add(number)
        if course_id not in last_read:  # rows are newest-first
            last_read[course_id] = (number, title)
        _offer(course_id, when, number)

    subs = db.execute(
        select(Activity.course_id, Submission.created_at, Activity.chapter_number)
        .join(
            Activity,
            (Activity.id == Submission.activity_id)
            & (Activity.tenant_id == Submission.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(Submission.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Submission.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Activity.course_id.in_(course_ids))
    ).all()
    for course_id, when, chapter_number in subs:
        _offer(course_id, when, chapter_number)

    atts = db.execute(
        select(Activity.course_id, ActivityAttempt.started_at, Activity.chapter_number)
        .join(
            Activity,
            (Activity.id == ActivityAttempt.activity_id)
            & (Activity.tenant_id == ActivityAttempt.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(ActivityAttempt.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(ActivityAttempt.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Activity.course_id.in_(course_ids))
    ).all()
    for course_id, when, chapter_number in atts:
        _offer(course_id, when, chapter_number)

    return {
        "last_touch": last_touch,
        "last_read": last_read,
        "read_numbers": read_numbers,
    }


def _due_by_offering(
    db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, offering_ids: Sequence[UUID]
) -> dict[UUID, list[tuple[UUID, datetime | None]]]:
    """All (activity_id, due_at) pacing rows grouped by offering, in ONE query."""
    if not offering_ids:
        return {}
    rows = db.execute(
        select(
            OfferingActivity.offering_id,
            OfferingActivity.activity_id,
            OfferingActivity.due_at,
        )
        .where(OfferingActivity.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(OfferingActivity.offering_id.in_(offering_ids))
    ).all()
    out: dict[UUID, list[tuple[UUID, datetime | None]]] = {}
    for offering_id, activity_id, due in rows:
        out.setdefault(offering_id, []).append((activity_id, due))
    return out


def _resume_from(
    chapters: list[ChapterFact],
    activities: list[ActivityFact],
    best: dict[UUID, ScoreFact],
    read_numbers: set[int],
    last_touch: tuple[datetime, int] | None,
) -> ChapterFact | None:
    """Pure resume computation from already-fetched data (no queries)."""
    if not chapters:
        return None
    passed_acts = {aid for aid, s in best.items() if s.passed}
    acts_by_chapter: dict[int, list[ActivityFact]] = {}
    for a in activities:
        if a.chapter_number is None:
            continue
        acts_by_chapter.setdefault(a.chapter_number, []).append(a)

    def incomplete(ch: ChapterFact) -> bool:
        acts = acts_by_chapter.get(ch.number, [])
        acts_done = all(a.id in passed_acts for a in acts) if acts else True
        return not (acts_done and ch.number in read_numbers)

    start_number = last_touch[1] if last_touch is not None else chapters[0].number
    ordered = [c for c in chapters if c.number >= start_number] + [
        c for c in chapters if c.number < start_number
    ]
    for ch in ordered:
        if incomplete(ch):
            return ch
    return None


def resume_chapter(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, course_id: UUID
) -> ChapterFact | None:
    """The chapter to resume at: the first incomplete chapter at or after the
    last touched one (wrapping to the start), or None when nothing remains.

    Public single-course entry point (unchanged signature); the batched
    dashboard path uses :func:`_resume_from` with already-fetched data.
    """
    chapters = _chapters(db, tenant_id, course_id)
    if not chapters:
        return None
    best = best_scores_for(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, course_id=course_id
    )
    bundle = _touch_bundle(db, tenant_id, person_id, [course_id])
    return _resume_from(
        chapters,
        _activities(db, tenant_id, course_id),
        best,
        bundle["read_numbers"].get(course_id, set()),
        bundle["last_touch"].get(course_id),
    )


def continue_target(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    _ctx: _DashboardContext | None = None,
) -> ContinueTarget | None:
    """Cross-course resume: the most recently touched course's resume chapter.

    ``_ctx`` (from :func:`_dashboard_context`) lets ``learner_home`` share the
    already-computed touch/activity data so the ``/`` render fans out once, not
    twice (roadmap review item 5). Standalone callers pass nothing.
    """
    if _ctx is not None:
        pairs = _ctx["pairs"]
    else:
        pairs = _entitled_courses(db, tenant_id, person_id)
    if not pairs:
        return None
    courses_by_id = {c.id: c for c, _ in pairs}
    course_ids = [c.id for c, _ in pairs]
    bundle = (
        _ctx["bundle"]
        if _ctx is not None
        else _touch_bundle(db, tenant_id, person_id, course_ids)
    )
    last_touch = bundle["last_touch"]
    latest_course_id = None
    latest_when = None
    for cid in course_ids:
        t = last_touch.get(cid)
        if t is not None and (latest_when is None or t[0] > latest_when):
            latest_when, latest_course_id = t[0], cid
    if latest_course_id is None:
        return None
    if _ctx is not None:
        chapter = _resume_from(
            _ctx["chapters_by_course"].get(latest_course_id, []),
            _ctx["activities_by_course"].get(latest_course_id, []),
            _ctx["best"],
            bundle["read_numbers"].get(latest_course_id, set()),
            last_touch.get(latest_course_id),
        )
    else:
        chapter = resume_chapter(
            db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, course_id=latest_course_id
        )
    if chapter is None:
        return None
    return ContinueTarget(courses_by_id[latest_course_id], chapter)


def _next_deadline_from(
    due_rows: list[tuple[UUID, datetime | None]],
    ends_at: datetime | None,
    now: datetime,
) -> datetime | None:
    """Earliest future deadline from already-fetched (activity_id, due) rows."""
    deadlines = [due for _aid, due in due_rows if due is not None and due > now]
    if ends_at is not None and ends_at > now:
        deadlines.append(ends_at)
    return min(deadlines) if deadlines else None


def _dashboard_context(
    db: Session, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, now: datetime | None
) -> _DashboardContext:
    """All batched inputs the dashboard + cross-course resume share, fetched
    once (bounded query count) so ``home()`` never recomputes per course."""
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    pairs = _entitled_courses(db, tenant_id, person_id)
    course_ids = [c.id for c, _ in pairs]
    offering_ids = [o.id for _, o in pairs]
    sessions = scheduling.list_for_person(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, now=now
    )
    next_session_by_cohort: dict[UUID, ClassSessionFact] = {}
    for entry in sessions.upcoming:
        session = entry.session
        next_session_by_cohort.setdefault(session.cohort_id, session)
    return {
        "now": now,
        "pairs": pairs,
        "course_ids": course_ids,
        "offering_ids": offering_ids,
        "access": course_access_states(db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id),

def course_cards(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    now: datetime | None = None,
    _ctx: _DashboardContext | None = None,
) -> CourseCards:
    """The My Courses projection: cards with one state and one action each.

    Returns detached cards, ordered state counts and semantic filter codes.
    """
    ctx = (
        _ctx if _ctx is not None else _dashboard_context(db, tenant_id, person_id, now)
    )
    now = ctx["now"]
    pairs = ctx["pairs"]
    access = ctx["access"]
    completions = ctx["completions"]
    certificates = ctx["certificates"]
    next_session_by_cohort = ctx["next_session_by_cohort"]
    activities_by_course = ctx["activities_by_course"]
    best = ctx["best"]
    bundle = ctx["bundle"]
    chapters_by_course = ctx["chapters_by_course"]
    due_by_offering = ctx["due_by_offering"]
    last_touch = bundle["last_touch"]
    last_read = bundle["last_read"]
    read_numbers = bundle["read_numbers"]

    cards: list[CourseCard] = []
    counts: dict[CardState, int] = dict.fromkeys(_STATES, 0)
    for course, offering in pairs:
        activities = activities_by_course.get(course.id, [])
        total = len(activities)
        passed = sum(1 for a in activities if a.id in best and best[a.id].passed)
        pct = round(100 * passed / total) if total else 0
        grade = grade_from(activities, best)
        final_threshold = max((a.pass_threshold for a in activities), default=0.0)

        completion = completions.get(course.id)
        state_info = access.get(course.id)
        touch = last_touch.get(course.id)

        state: CardState
        if state_info is not None and state_info.locked:
            state = "locked"
        elif offering.starts_at is not None and offering.starts_at > now:
            state = "upcoming"
        elif completion is not None and completion.status == "completed":
            state = "completed"
        else:
            effective_ends_at = offering.effective_ends_at
            state = (
                "expired"
                if effective_ends_at is not None and effective_ends_at < now
                else "in_progress"
            )
        counts[state] += 1

        next_activity = next(
            (a for a in activities if a.id not in best or not best[a.id].passed), None
        )
        read_row = last_read.get(course.id)

        certificate = certificates.get(course.id)
        cert_status: CertificateStatus | None
        if certificate is not None:
            cert_status = "issued"
        elif state == "completed":
            cert_status = "eligible"
        else:
            cert_status = None

        action: DashboardAction | None = None
        if state == "in_progress":
            if touch is None:
                action = DashboardAction("start", course.id, 1)
            else:
                target = _resume_from(
                    chapters_by_course.get(course.id, []),
                    activities,
                    best,
                    read_numbers.get(course.id, set()),
                    touch,
                )
                number = target.number if target is not None else 1
                action = DashboardAction("resume", course.id, number)
        elif state == "completed":
            action = DashboardAction("review_feedback", course.id)

        cards.append(
            CourseCard(
                course,
                state,
                pct,
                passed,
                total,
                grade.pct,
                int(round(final_threshold * 100)),
                next_activity,
                _next_deadline_from(
                    due_by_offering.get(offering.id, []),
                    offering.effective_ends_at,
                    now,
                ),
                offering.starts_at,
                LastRead(*read_row) if read_row is not None else None,
                next_session_by_cohort.get(offering.cohort_id),
                cert_status,
                state_info.locked_reason
                if state_info is not None and state_info.locked
                else None,
                action,
            )
        )
    return CourseCards(
        tuple(cards), tuple(StateCount(s, counts[s]) for s in _STATES), _STATES
    )


def _trend(points: list[int]) -> Trend:
    if len(points) < 3:
        return "flat"
    half = len(points) // 2
    earlier = sum(points[:half]) / half
    later = sum(points[half:]) / (len(points) - half)
    if later - earlier > 3:
        return "up"
    if earlier - later > 3:
        return "down"
    return "flat"


def _due_key(row: ProgressActivity) -> datetime:
    # Only rows with future, non-null due dates enter the upcoming collection.
    if row.due_at is None:
        raise AssertionError
    return row.due_at


def progress_overview(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, now: datetime | None = None
) -> tuple[CourseProgress, ...]:
    """The rich per-course progress projection for /progress."""
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    pairs = _entitled_courses(db, tenant_id, person_id)
    course_ids = [c.id for c, _ in pairs]
    offering_ids = [o.id for _, o in pairs]

    # Batched fan-out (roadmap review item 5).
    activities_by_course = _activities_by_course(db, tenant_id, course_ids)
    best = best_scores_for_person(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id, course_ids=course_ids
    )
    attempts_by_activity = attempts_used_by_person(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id
    )
    grants_by_activity = attempt_policy.granted_by_activity(
        db, tenant_id=tenant_id, person_id=person_id
    )
    due_rows_by_offering = _due_by_offering(db, tenant_id, offering_ids)
    completions = {
        c.course_id: _completion_fact(c)
        for c in db.scalars(
            select(CourseCompletion)
            .where(CourseCompletion.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(CourseCompletion.person_id == person_id)
        ).all()
    }
    certificates = {
        c.course_id: _certificate_fact(c)
        for c in db.scalars(
            select(Certificate)
            .where(Certificate.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(Certificate.person_id == person_id)
        ).all()
    }
    # Trend points: every score across the person's courses, ordered, grouped.
    trend_by_course: dict[UUID, list[int]] = {}
    for course_id, fraction in db.execute(
        select(Activity.course_id, Score.fraction)
        .join(
            Submission,
            (Submission.id == Score.submission_id)
            & (Submission.tenant_id == Score.tenant_id),
        )
        .join(
            Activity,
            (Activity.id == Submission.activity_id)
            & (Activity.tenant_id == Submission.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(Score.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Submission.person_id == person_id)
        .where(
            Activity.course_id.in_(course_ids)
            if course_ids
            else Activity.course_id.is_(None)
        )
        .order_by(Score.created_at.asc())
    ).all():
        trend_by_course.setdefault(course_id, []).append(round(100 * fraction))

    out: list[CourseProgress] = []
    for course, offering in pairs:
        activities = activities_by_course.get(course.id, [])
        grade = grade_from(activities, best)
        due_by_activity = dict(due_rows_by_offering.get(offering.id, []))

        rows: list[ProgressActivity] = []
        upcoming: list[ProgressActivity] = []
        overdue: list[ProgressActivity] = []
        for a in activities:
            score = best.get(a.id)
            used = attempts_by_activity.get(a.id, 0)
            ent = attempt_policy.entitlement(
                a, used=used, granted=grants_by_activity.get(a.id, 0)
            )
            remaining = ent.remaining
            due = due_by_activity.get(a.id) or offering.ends_at
            is_passed = score is not None and score.passed
            is_overdue = due is not None and due < now and not is_passed
            row = ProgressActivity(
                a,
                a.chapter_number,
                score,
                round(100 * score.fraction) if score is not None else None,
                is_passed,
                int(round(a.pass_threshold * 100)),
                used,
                ent.limit,
                remaining,
                ent.granted,
                score is not None
                and reveal_feedback(
                    a,
                    passed=score.passed,
                    attempts_used=used,
                    attempts_granted=ent.granted,
                ),
                due,
                is_overdue,
            )
            rows.append(row)
            if is_overdue:
                overdue.append(row)
            elif due is not None and due > now and not is_passed:
                upcoming.append(row)

        score_points = trend_by_course.get(course.id, [])[-8:]

        completion = completions.get(course.id)
        certificate = certificates.get(course.id)
        completed = completion is not None and completion.status == "completed"

        out.append(
            CourseProgress(
                course,
                grade.pct,
                round(100 * completion.pct) if completion is not None else 0,
                int(
                    round(
                        max((a.pass_threshold for a in activities), default=0.0) * 100
                    )
                ),
                tuple(rows),
                tuple(sorted(upcoming, key=_due_key)),
                tuple(overdue),
                tuple(score_points),
                _trend(score_points),
                ProgressCertificate(
                    "issued"
                    if certificate is not None
                    else ("eligible" if completed else None),
                    certificate.serial if certificate is not None else None,
                    course.id if completed else None,
                ),
            )
        )
    return tuple(out)

"""Academy 096 per-activity pacing reads and enforcement.

Offering windows are enforced by the product's course-access owner. This owner
only reads applicable overrides; the audited source has no production writer.
Ordinary ORM autoflush and caller-owned transaction behavior are retained.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .delivery_models import OfferingActivity
from .pacing_contracts import PacingFact, PacingForbidden
from .participation_models import CourseOffering, Enrollment


def _applicable_overrides(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, course_id: UUID, activity_id: UUID
) -> list[OfferingActivity]:
    """Activity overrides across the person's active offerings, of any role."""
    return list(
        db.scalars(
            select(OfferingActivity)
            .join(
                CourseOffering,
                (CourseOffering.id == OfferingActivity.offering_id)
                & (CourseOffering.tenant_id == OfferingActivity.tenant_id),
            )
            .join(
                Enrollment,
                (Enrollment.cohort_id == CourseOffering.cohort_id)
                & (Enrollment.tenant_id == CourseOffering.tenant_id),
            )
            .where(OfferingActivity.tenant_id == tenant_id)
            .where(OfferingActivity.activity_id == activity_id)
            .where(CourseOffering.course_id == course_id)
            .where(CourseOffering.status == "active")
            .where(Enrollment.person_id == person_id)
            .where(Enrollment.status == "active")
        ).all()
    )


def activity_pacing(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    course_id: UUID,
    activity_id: UUID,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> PacingFact:
    """Return the most permissive applicable release/submission decision."""
    now = now or datetime.now(UTC)
    overrides = _applicable_overrides(
        db,
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        person_id=person_id,
        course_id=course_id,
        activity_id=activity_id,
    )
    if not overrides:
        return PacingFact(readable=True, submittable=True, has_override=False)

    readable = False
    submittable = False
    for ov in overrides:
        released = ov.release_at is None or ov.release_at <= now
        not_past_due = ov.due_at is None or ov.due_at >= now
        readable = readable or released
        submittable = submittable or (released and not_past_due)
    return PacingFact(readable=readable, submittable=submittable, has_override=True)


def require_activity_readable(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    course_id: UUID,
    activity_id: UUID,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> None:
    fact = activity_pacing(
        db,
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        person_id=person_id,
        course_id=course_id,
        activity_id=activity_id,
        now=now,
    )
    if not fact.readable:
        raise PacingForbidden("Activity not yet released")


def require_activity_submittable(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    course_id: UUID,
    activity_id: UUID,
    now: datetime | None = None,
) -> None:
    fact = activity_pacing(
        db,
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        person_id=person_id,
        course_id=course_id,
        activity_id=activity_id,
        now=now,
    )
    if not fact.submittable:
        raise PacingForbidden(
            "Activity is not open for submission (not released or past due)"
        )


__all__ = [
    "activity_pacing",
    "require_activity_readable",
    "require_activity_submittable",
]

_PARTICIPATION_ROW_TYPES = (
    ("cohorts", CohortRowV3),
    ("enrollments", EnrollmentRowV3),
    ("tracks", TrackRowV3),
    ("track_courses", TrackCourseRowV3),
    ("cohort_tracks", CohortTrackRowV3),
    ("course_offerings", CourseOfferingRowV3),
    ("course_prerequisites", CoursePrerequisiteRowV3),
)


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, repr=False)
class LearningSnapshotV3:
    """Full CURRENT selected extent, including explicitly empty tables."""

    version: Literal[3]
    tenant_ids: tuple[UUID, ...]
    courses: tuple[CourseRowV1, ...]
    activities: tuple[ActivityRowV1, ...]
    submissions: tuple[SubmissionRowV1, ...]
    scores: tuple[ScoreRowV1, ...]
    course_completions: tuple[CourseCompletionRowV1, ...]
    certificates: tuple[CertificateRowV1, ...]
    learning_events: tuple[LearningEventRowV1, ...]
    chapters: tuple[_v2.ChapterRowV2, ...]
    question_banks: tuple[_v2.QuestionBankRowV2, ...]
    questions: tuple[_v2.QuestionRowV2, ...]
    chapter_reads: tuple[_v2.ChapterReadRowV2, ...]
    subtopic_reads: tuple[_v2.SubtopicReadRowV2, ...]
    chapter_bookmarks: tuple[_v2.ChapterBookmarkRowV2, ...]
    chapter_notes: tuple[_v2.ChapterNoteRowV2, ...]
    cohorts: tuple[CohortRowV3, ...]
    enrollments: tuple[EnrollmentRowV3, ...]
    tracks: tuple[TrackRowV3, ...]
    track_courses: tuple[TrackCourseRowV3, ...]
    cohort_tracks: tuple[CohortTrackRowV3, ...]
    course_offerings: tuple[CourseOfferingRowV3, ...]
    course_prerequisites: tuple[CoursePrerequisiteRowV3, ...]

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if type(self.version) is not int or self.version != 3:
            raise SnapshotValidationError(
                "unsupported twenty-one-table snapshot version"
            )
        _curriculum_slice(self)
        extent = set(self.tenant_ids)
        for table, row_type in _PARTICIPATION_ROW_TYPES:
            rows = getattr(self, table)
            if type(rows) is not tuple:
                raise SnapshotValidationError(f"storage rows must be a tuple: {table}")
            keys: set[UUID] = set()
            for row in rows:
                if type(row) is not row_type:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"wrong storage row contract: {table}"
                    )
                row.__post_init__()
                if row.tenant_id not in extent:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"storage row outside declared extent: {table}/{row.id}"
                    )
                if row.id in keys:
                    raise SnapshotValidationError(
                        f"duplicate storage key: {table}/{row.id}"
                    )
                keys.add(row.id)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return "LearningSnapshotV3(<twenty-one-table storage rows>)"


def _curriculum_slice(snapshot: LearningSnapshotV3) -> _v2.LearningSnapshotV2:
    """Internal fourteen-table projection; does not prove full V3 scope."""
    return _v2.LearningSnapshotV2(
        version=2,
        tenant_ids=snapshot.tenant_ids,
        courses=snapshot.courses,
        activities=snapshot.activities,
        submissions=snapshot.submissions,
        scores=snapshot.scores,
        course_completions=snapshot.course_completions,
        certificates=snapshot.certificates,
        learning_events=snapshot.learning_events,
        chapters=snapshot.chapters,
        question_banks=snapshot.question_banks,
        questions=snapshot.questions,
        chapter_reads=snapshot.chapter_reads,
        subtopic_reads=snapshot.subtopic_reads,
        chapter_bookmarks=snapshot.chapter_bookmarks,
        chapter_notes=snapshot.chapter_notes,
    )


class SnapshotClosureErrorV3(SnapshotValidationError):
    """A missing actual FK parent, with child location and no payload values."""

    def __init__(self, table: str, key: UUID, column: str) -> None:
        self.table, self.key, self.column = table, key, column
        super().__init__(f"unclosed storage reference: {table}/{key}/{column}")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class VerificationObservationV3:
    """Uncommitted exact full-table observation, never completeness authority."""

    version: Literal[3]
    tenant_ids: tuple[UUID, ...]
    row_counts: tuple[RowCountObservation, ...]

    @property
    def matched(self) -> Literal[True]:
        return True


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ImportObservationV3:
    """Uncommitted twenty-one-table inserts and independent exact readback."""

    version: Literal[3]
    verification: VerificationObservationV3
    inserted_rows: tuple[RowCountObservation, ...]

def _course_fact(row: Course) -> CourseFact:

        **{field: getattr(row, field) for field in CourseFact.__dataclass_fields__}
    )

        **{field: getattr(row, field) for field in ActivityFact.__dataclass_fields__}
    )


def get_course(db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, course_id: UUID) -> CourseFact | None:
    row = db.scalar(
        select(Course)
        .where(Course.tenant_id == tenant_id, Course.id == course_id)
        .execution_options(populate_existing=True)
    )
    return _course_fact(row) if row is not None else None

) -> ActivityFact | None:

    )
    return _activity_fact(row) if row is not None else None


def create_course(db: Session, payload: CourseWrite) -> CourseFact:
    row = Course(**payload.model_dump())
    db.add(row)
    db.flush()
    return _course_fact(row)


def update_course(db: Session, payload: CourseWrite) -> CourseFact:
    """Replace supplied reference fields; product has already decided the change."""
    row = db.scalar(
        select(Course).where(
            Course.tenant_id == payload.tenant_id, Course.id == payload.id
        )
    )
    if row is None:
        raise ReferenceNotFound("course not found for tenant")
    for name, value in payload.model_dump(exclude={"id", "tenant_id"}).items():
        setattr(row, name, value)
    db.flush()
    return _course_fact(row)

"""Six independent Academy reminder input reads in the caller's Session.

Product code supplies the source time bounds and interleaves these reads with
canonical todo, scheduling and event reads. Reminder occurrence order, keys,
copy, inactivity windows, delivery preferences and ReminderLog stay in Academy.
These functions neither select recipients nor establish a population snapshot.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime
from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import func, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .models import Activity, Certificate, Course, CourseCompletion, Score, Submission
from .participation_models import Cohort, CourseOffering, Enrollment
from .reminder_contracts import (
    OpeningOffering,
    RecentAssignment,
    RecentCertificate,
    RecentCompletedCourse,
    RecentManualResult,
)


def recent_assignments(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, since: datetime
) -> tuple[RecentAssignment, ...]:
    """Active enrollments of any role created at or after the supplied bound."""
    rows = db.execute(
        select(Enrollment.id, Cohort.name)
        .join(
            Cohort,
            (Cohort.id == Enrollment.cohort_id)
            & (Cohort.tenant_id == Enrollment.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(Enrollment.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Enrollment.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Enrollment.status == "active")
        .where(Enrollment.created_at >= since)
    ).all()
    return tuple(RecentAssignment(enrollment_id, name) for enrollment_id, name in rows)


def opening_offerings(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tenant_id: UUID,
    person_id: UUID,
    after: datetime,
    through: datetime,
) -> tuple[OpeningOffering, ...]:
    """Active offerings with starts strictly after and inclusively through bounds.

    Preserve the source enrollment join, multiplicity and unspecified SQL order.
    No course-publication, cohort-status or enrollment-role selector is added.
    """
    rows = db.execute(
        select(CourseOffering.id, Course.title, CourseOffering.starts_at)
        .join(
            Course,
            (Course.id == CourseOffering.course_id)
            & (Course.tenant_id == CourseOffering.tenant_id),
        )
        .join(
            Enrollment,
            (Enrollment.cohort_id == CourseOffering.cohort_id)
            & (Enrollment.tenant_id == CourseOffering.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(CourseOffering.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Enrollment.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Enrollment.status == "active")
        .where(CourseOffering.status == "active")
        .where(CourseOffering.starts_at.is_not(None))
        .where(CourseOffering.starts_at > after)
        .where(CourseOffering.starts_at <= through)
    ).all()
    result: list[OpeningOffering] = []
    for offering_id, title, starts_at in rows:
        if starts_at is None:
            raise AssertionError
        result.append(OpeningOffering(offering_id, title, starts_at))
    return tuple(result)


def recent_manual_results(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, since: datetime
) -> tuple[RecentManualResult, ...]:
    """Every recent non-auto Score, including failures and multiple per submission.

    Source != 'auto' is retained with SQL's null behavior. 'Manual' in this
    projection's name does not restrict storage to a particular source code.
    """
    rows = db.execute(
        select(Score.id, Activity.title)
        .join(
            Submission,
            (Submission.id == Score.submission_id)
            & (Submission.tenant_id == Score.tenant_id),
        )
        .join(
            Activity,
            (Activity.id == Submission.activity_id)
            & (Activity.tenant_id == Submission.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(Score.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Submission.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Score.source != "auto")
        .where(Score.created_at >= since)
    ).all()
    return tuple(RecentManualResult(score_id, title) for score_id, title in rows)


def recent_completed_courses(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, since: datetime
) -> tuple[RecentCompletedCourse, ...]:
    """Completed records with a non-null completion timestamp at or after since."""
    rows = db.execute(
        select(CourseCompletion.id, Course.title)
        .join(
            Course,
            (Course.id == CourseCompletion.course_id)
            & (Course.tenant_id == CourseCompletion.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(CourseCompletion.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(CourseCompletion.person_id == person_id)
        .where(CourseCompletion.status == "completed")
        .where(CourseCompletion.completed_at.is_not(None))
        .where(CourseCompletion.completed_at >= since)
    ).all()
    return tuple(
        RecentCompletedCourse(completion_id, title) for completion_id, title in rows
    )


def recent_certificates(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID, since: datetime
) -> tuple[RecentCertificate, ...]:
    """Certificates issued at or after since; no expiration policy is invented."""
    rows = db.execute(
        select(Certificate.id, Course.title)
        .join(
            Course,
            (Course.id == Certificate.course_id)
            & (Course.tenant_id == Certificate.tenant_id),
        )
        .where(Certificate.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Certificate.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Certificate.issued_at >= since)
    ).all()
    return tuple(
        RecentCertificate(certificate_id, title) for certificate_id, title in rows
    )


def earliest_active_enrollment_at(
    db: Session, *, tenant_id: UUID, person_id: UUID
) -> datetime | None:
    """Earliest active enrollment of any role, for the caller's no-event fallback.

    Academy calls this only when events.last_activity_at has returned None; this
    read owns neither that interleaving nor inactivity cutoffs/counts/windows.
    """
    return db.scalar(
        select(func.min(Enrollment.created_at))
        .where(Enrollment.tenant_id == tenant_id)
        .where(Enrollment.person_id == person_id)
        .where(Enrollment.status == "active")
    )
